23: /// Signal emitted after a leaf is admitted and marked queryable.

27:     pub kind: &'static str,

40:             item_id: item_id.into(),
41:             bank_id: bank_id.into(),
42:         }
43:     }
44: }

46: /// Consumer for dirty-path refresh (slice 100070 may subscribe). Must not block writers.
47: pub trait MaintenanceHook: std::fmt::Debug {

49:     fn on_leaf_attached(&self, signal: MaintenanceSignal);
50: }

52: /// No-op hook when no maintenance subscriber is present.
53: #[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
54: pub struct NoopMaintenance;

57:     fn on_leaf_attached(&self, _signal: MaintenanceSignal) {}
58: }

62: pub struct BufferMaintenance {
63:     signals: Mutex<Vec<MaintenanceSignal>>,
64: }
65: 
66: impl BufferMaintenance {
67:     /// Snapshot of buffered signals.
68:     #[must_use]
69:     pub fn signals(&self) -> Vec<MaintenanceSignal> {
70:         self.signals.lock().expect("maintenance buffer").clone()
71:     }
72: }
73: 
74: impl MaintenanceHook for BufferMaintenance {
75:     fn on_leaf_attached(&self, signal: MaintenanceSignal) {
76:         self.signals

78:             .expect("maintenance buffer")
79:             .push(signal);
80:     }

100:     }

104:     pub fn get(&self, bank_id: &str, item_id: &str) -> Option<MemoryItem> {
105:         self.items

288: ) -> Result<IngestOutcome, AmError> {
289:     bank_guard(args.ctx, &args.item_base)?;
290:     if args.config.embedding_merge {
291:         return Err(AmError::new(
292:             ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
293:             "embedding_merge must stay off until dense index exists; deterministic fingerprint is the merge authority",
294:         ));
295:     }
296: 
297:     let t0 = Instant::now();
298:     let profile = args.config.profile_label.as_str();
299:     let chunks = partition_session(args.turns, args.config.max_turns_per_chunk);
300:     if chunks.is_empty() {
301:         return Ok(empty_outcome(profile, t0, 0, vec![], vec![]));
302:     }
303: 
304:     let t_extract = Instant::now();
305:     let agg = extract_chunks_parallel(
306:         args.extractor,
307:         &chunks,
308:         &args.schema_template,
309:         args.fields,

311:         args.config.concurrency,
312:     );
313:     let extract_phase_ms = t_extract.elapsed().as_millis();
314:     let retained: Vec<_> = agg
315:         .results
316:         .iter()
317:         .filter_map(|r| r.retained.clone())
318:         .collect();
319: 
320:     let abort_all = args.config.all_or_nothing
321:         && (agg.refused_count > 0 || agg.error_count > 0 || agg.verified_count < chunks.len());
322:     if abort_all {
323:         return Ok(empty_outcome(
324:             profile,
325:             t0,
326:             extract_phase_ms,
327:             agg.results,
328:             retained,
329:         ));

27: /// Verified extract candidate awaiting consolidation.

30:     /// Source chunk id.
31:     pub chunk_id: String,
32:     /// Span haystack for this candidate.

45:     /// Merged gist (non-authoritative).

56:     pub discrete_key: Option<String>,
57:     /// True when this unit was kept separate due to a contradictory object.
58:     pub contradiction_split: bool,

60:     pub triple_handoff_note: Option<String>,

83: /// NFC + lowercase + collapse whitespace for surface forms.

85: pub fn normalize_surface(s: &str) -> String {
86:     let nfc: String = s.nfc().collect();

88:         .map(str::to_lowercase)
89:         .collect::<Vec<_>>()
90:         .join(" ")

93: fn normalize_value(v: &Value) -> Value {
94:     match v {
95:         Value::String(s) => Value::String(normalize_surface(s)),
96:         Value::Array(arr) => Value::Array(arr.iter().map(normalize_value).collect()),
97:         Value::Object(map) => {
98:             let mut out = Map::new();
99:             let mut keys: Vec<_> = map.keys().cloned().collect();
100:             keys.sort();
101:             for k in keys {
102:                 if let Some(val) = map.get(&k) {
103:                     out.insert(k, normalize_value(val));
104:                 }
105:             }
106:             Value::Object(out)
107:         }
108:         other => other.clone(),
109:     }
110: }

112: /// Deterministic fingerprint over the normalized snapshot (or gist fallback).
113: #[must_use]
114: pub fn fingerprint(candidate: &ExtractCandidate) -> u64 {
115:     let payload = if let Some(snap) = &candidate.snapshot {
116:         normalize_value(snap)
117:     } else {
118:         Value::String(normalize_surface(candidate.gist.as_deref().unwrap_or("")))
119:     };
120:     let mut hasher = std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher::new();
121:     serde_json::to_string(&payload)
122:         .unwrap_or_default()
123:         .hash(&mut hasher);
124:     hasher.finish()
125: }
126: 
127: fn str_field(snap: &Value, keys: &[&str]) -> Option<String> {
128:     let obj = snap.as_object()?;
129:     for k in keys {
130:         if let Some(Value::String(s)) = obj.get(*k) {
131:             let n = normalize_surface(s);
132:             if !n.is_empty() {
133:                 return Some(n);
134:             }
135:         }
136:     }
137:     None
138: }

140: /// Discrete key for SPO-shaped or explicit attribute snapshots.
141: ///
142: /// Forms recognized:
143: /// - `subject`+`predicate` (aliases `s`/`p`)
144: /// - `attribute` / `attr` / `key` as a single discrete attribute key
145: #[must_use]
146: pub fn discrete_key(snapshot: &Value) -> Option<String> {
147:     if let (Some(sub), Some(pred)) = (
148:         str_field(snapshot, &["subject", "s"]),
149:         str_field(snapshot, &["predicate", "p", "rel", "relation"]),
150:     ) {
151:         return Some(format!("{sub}|{pred}"));
152:     }
153:     str_field(snapshot, &["attribute", "attr", "key"]).map(|a| format!("attr:{a}"))
154: }
155: 
156: fn discrete_object(snapshot: &Value) -> Option<String> {
157:     str_field(snapshot, &["object", "o", "value", "val"])
158: }

160: fn confidence_of(c: &VerifiedCandidate) -> f64 {
161:     if (0.0..=1.0).contains(&c.confidence) {
162:         c.confidence
163:     } else {
164:         1.0
165:     }
166: }

168: fn unit_from(
169:     c: &VerifiedCandidate,
170:     contradiction_split: bool,
171:     note: Option<String>,
172: ) -> CanonicalUnit {
173:     CanonicalUnit {
174:         snapshot: c.candidate.snapshot.clone(),
175:         gist: c.candidate.gist.clone(),
176:         source_refs: vec![c.candidate.source_ref.clone()],
177:         chunk_ids: vec![c.chunk_id.clone()],
178:         source_text: c.source_text.clone(),
179:         confidence: confidence_of(c),
180:         discrete_key: c.candidate.snapshot.as_ref().and_then(discrete_key),
181:         contradiction_split,
182:         triple_handoff_note: note,
183:     }
184: }
185: 
186: fn merge_into(unit: &mut CanonicalUnit, c: &VerifiedCandidate) {
187:     if unit.gist.as_ref().map_or(0, String::len) < c.candidate.gist.as_ref().map_or(0, String::len)
188:     {
189:         unit.gist.clone_from(&c.candidate.gist);
190:     }
191:     if !unit.source_refs.contains(&c.candidate.source_ref) {
192:         unit.source_refs.push(c.candidate.source_ref.clone());
193:     }
194:     if !unit.chunk_ids.contains(&c.chunk_id) {
195:         unit.chunk_ids.push(c.chunk_id.clone());
196:     }
197:     if !unit.source_text.contains(&c.source_text) {
198:         unit.source_text = format!("{}\n{}", unit.source_text, c.source_text);
199:     }
200:     unit.confidence = unit.confidence.max(confidence_of(c));
201: }
202: 
203: /// Merge near-duplicates by deterministic fingerprint; never blend discrete contradictions.
204: ///
205: /// Embedding/LLM merge is intentionally absent from the default path.
206: #[must_use]
207: pub fn consolidate(candidates: &[VerifiedCandidate]) -> ConsolidateResult {
208:     let mut units: Vec<CanonicalUnit> = Vec::new();
209:     // fingerprint → unit index (non-keyed or matching-object keyed)
210:     let mut by_fp: BTreeMap<u64, usize> = BTreeMap::new();
211:     // discrete key → (object_norm, unit index)
212:     let mut by_key: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(String, usize)>> = BTreeMap::new();
213:     let mut stats = ConsolidateStats::default();
214: 
215:     for c in candidates {
216:         let fp = fingerprint(&c.candidate);
217:         let key = c.candidate.snapshot.as_ref().and_then(discrete_key);
218:         let obj = c
219:             .candidate
220:             .snapshot
221:             .as_ref()
222:             .and_then(discrete_object)
223:             .unwrap_or_default();
224: 
225:         if let Some(ref dk) = key {
226:             let entries = by_key.entry(dk.clone()).or_default();
227:             if let Some((_, idx)) = entries.iter().find(|(o, _)| o == &obj) {
228:                 merge_into(&mut units[*idx], c);
229:                 stats.merges += 1;
230:                 continue;
231:             }
232:             if !entries.is_empty() && !obj.is_empty() {
233:                 // Same discrete key, different object → separate unit + handoff note.
234:                 let note = Some(format!(
235:                     "discrete_key_contradiction:{dk}; handoff=triple_supersession"
236:                 ));
237:                 let idx = units.len();
238:                 units.push(unit_from(c, true, note));
239:                 entries.push((obj, idx));
240:                 stats.contradiction_splits += 1;
241:                 continue;
242:             }
243:             let idx = units.len();
244:             units.push(unit_from(c, false, None));
245:             entries.push((obj, idx));
246:             by_fp.insert(fp, idx);
247:             continue;
248:         }
249: 
250:         if let Some(&idx) = by_fp.get(&fp) {
251:             merge_into(&mut units[idx], c);
252:             stats.merges += 1;
253:             continue;
254:         }
255:         let idx = units.len();
256:         units.push(unit_from(c, false, None));
257:         by_fp.insert(fp, idx);
258:     }
259: 
260:     stats.units = u32::try_from(units.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
261:     ConsolidateResult { units, stats }
262: }

4: //! # Responsibility
5: //!
6: //! This module is responsible for bounded-parallel chunk extract+verify fan-out.
7: //!
8: //! ## Owns
9: //! - Hard concurrency cap `P` over chunk workers
10: //! - Per-chunk result aggregation (verified / refused / transport error)
11: //!
12: //! ## Does not own
13: //! - Consolidation or gated admit

15: //! ## Boundary

19: use crate::chunk::Chunk;

26: use clio_types::AmError;

28: use std::sync::{Mutex, mpsc};
29: 
30: /// One chunk's extract+verify outcome.
31: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
32: pub struct ChunkWorkerResult {
33:     /// Chunk id.
34:     pub chunk_id: String,
35:     /// Source text used as span haystack.
36:     pub source_text: String,
37:     /// Verified candidate when ok.
38:     pub candidate: Option<ExtractCandidate>,
39:     /// Non-authoritative retention when verify refused.
40:     pub retained: Option<NonAuthoritativeRetention>,
41:     /// Transport / extract error message when the worker failed hard.
42:     pub error: Option<String>,
43:     /// Extract call count (0 when transport failed before extract).
44:     pub extract_calls: u32,
45: }
46: 
47: /// Aggregate of a parallel extract batch.
48: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
49: pub struct ParallelExtractAggregate {
50:     /// Per-chunk results in input order.
51:     pub results: Vec<ChunkWorkerResult>,
52:     /// Count of chunks that produced a verified candidate.
53:     pub verified_count: usize,
54:     /// Count of chunks that refused after verify.
55:     pub refused_count: usize,
56:     /// Count of chunks that hit transport/extract errors.
57:     pub error_count: usize,
58: }
59: 
60: impl ParallelExtractAggregate {
61:     /// Verified candidates with their source text and chunk id.
62:     #[must_use]
63:     pub fn verified(&self) -> Vec<(String, String, ExtractCandidate)> {
64:         self.results
65:             .iter()
66:             .filter_map(|r| {
67:                 r.candidate
68:                     .clone()
69:                     .map(|c| (r.chunk_id.clone(), r.source_text.clone(), c))
70:             })
71:             .collect()
72:     }
73: }
74: 
75: fn worker_result(
76:     chunk: &Chunk,
77:     outcome: Result<ExtractVerifyOutcome, AmError>,
78: ) -> ChunkWorkerResult {
79:     match outcome {
80:         Ok(o) => ChunkWorkerResult {
81:             chunk_id: chunk.chunk_id.clone(),
82:             source_text: chunk.source_text.clone(),
83:             candidate: o.candidate,
84:             retained: o.retained,
85:             error: None,
86:             extract_calls: o.extract_calls,
87:         },
88:         Err(e) => ChunkWorkerResult {
89:             chunk_id: chunk.chunk_id.clone(),
90:             source_text: chunk.source_text.clone(),
91:             candidate: None,
92:             retained: None,
93:             error: Some(e.message),
94:             extract_calls: 0,
95:         },
96:     }
97: }

99: /// Extract+verify each chunk with at most `concurrency` workers.
100: ///
101: /// Partial-success policy: failed chunks are recorded; they do not cancel siblings.
102: /// Callers that need all-or-nothing must inspect the aggregate and abort before admit.
103: /// Per-chunk verify telemetry is omitted here (workers are multi-threaded); ingest
104: /// records aggregate merge/admit counts instead.
105: pub fn extract_chunks_parallel(
106:     extractor: &(dyn Extractor + Sync),
107:     chunks: &[Chunk],
108:     schema_template: &Value,
109:     fields: &[FieldSpec],
110:     verify: &VerifyConfig,
111:     concurrency: usize,
112: ) -> ParallelExtractAggregate {
113:     if chunks.is_empty() {
114:         return ParallelExtractAggregate {
115:             results: vec![],
116:             verified_count: 0,
117:             refused_count: 0,
118:             error_count: 0,
119:         };
120:     }
121:     let limit = concurrency.max(1).min(chunks.len());
122:     let work: Mutex<Vec<(usize, Chunk)>> = Mutex::new(
123:         chunks
124:             .iter()
125:             .cloned()
126:             .enumerate()
127:             .collect::<Vec<_>>()
128:             .into_iter()
129:             .rev()
130:             .collect(),
131:     );
132:     let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<(usize, ChunkWorkerResult)>();
133:     std::thread::scope(|scope| {
134:         for _ in 0..limit {
135:             let tx = tx.clone();
136:             let work = &work;
137:             scope.spawn(move || {
138:                 loop {
139:                     let next = work.lock().expect("work queue").pop();
140:                     let Some((idx, chunk)) = next else {
141:                         break;
142:                     };
143:                     let outcome = extract_and_verify(ExtractVerifyArgs {
144:                         extractor,
145:                         source_text: &chunk.source_text,
146:                         schema_template: schema_template.clone(),
147:                         tool_payload: chunk.tool_payload.clone(),
148:                         fields,
149:                         verify,
150:                         emit: None,
151:                     });
152:                     let _ = tx.send((idx, worker_result(&chunk, outcome)));
153:                 }
154:             });
155:         }
156:     });
157:     drop(tx);
158:     let mut pairs: Vec<(usize, ChunkWorkerResult)> = rx.into_iter().collect();
159:     pairs.sort_by_key(|(i, _)| *i);
160:     let results: Vec<ChunkWorkerResult> = pairs.into_iter().map(|(_, r)| r).collect();
161:     let verified_count = results.iter().filter(|r| r.candidate.is_some()).count();
162:     let refused_count = results
163:         .iter()
164:         .filter(|r| r.candidate.is_none() && r.error.is_none())
165:         .count();
166:     let error_count = results.iter().filter(|r| r.error.is_some()).count();
167:     ParallelExtractAggregate {
168:         results,
169:         verified_count,
170:         refused_count,
171:         error_count,
172:     }
173: }
174: 
175: /// Run `f` over `items` with at most `limit` concurrent threads (order-preserving).
176: pub fn map_bounded<T, R, F>(items: Vec<T>, limit: usize, f: F) -> Vec<R>
177: where
178:     T: Send,
179:     R: Send,
180:     F: Fn(T) -> R + Sync,
181: {
182:     if items.is_empty() {
183:         return Vec::new();
184:     }
185:     let n = items.len();
186:     let limit = limit.max(1).min(n);
187:     let work: Mutex<Vec<(usize, T)>> = Mutex::new(items.into_iter().enumerate().rev().collect());
188:     let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<(usize, R)>();
189:     std::thread::scope(|scope| {
190:         for _ in 0..limit {
191:             let tx = tx.clone();
192:             let work = &work;
193:             let f = &f;
194:             scope.spawn(move || {
195:                 loop {
196:                     let next = work.lock().expect("work").pop();
197:                     let Some((idx, item)) = next else {
198:                         break;
199:                     };
200:                     let _ = tx.send((idx, f(item)));
201:                 }
202:             });
203:         }
204:     });
205:     drop(tx);
206:     let mut pairs: Vec<(usize, R)> = rx.into_iter().collect();
207:     pairs.sort_by_key(|(i, _)| *i);
208:     pairs.into_iter().map(|(_, r)| r).collect()
209: }

57: /// Partition turns into extraction chunks of at most `max_turns_per_chunk`.
58: ///
59: /// Empty `source_text` turns are kept (caller may still fail verify later).
60: /// `max_turns_per_chunk` of 0 is treated as 1.
61: #[must_use]
62: pub fn partition_session(turns: &[Turn], max_turns_per_chunk: usize) -> Vec<Chunk> {
63:     if turns.is_empty() {
64:         return Vec::new();
65:     }
66:     let cap = max_turns_per_chunk.max(1);
67:     let mut out = Vec::new();
68:     let mut start = 0usize;
69:     while start < turns.len() {
70:         let end = (start + cap).min(turns.len());
71:         let slice = &turns[start..end];
72:         let source_text = slice
73:             .iter()
74:             .map(|t| t.source_text.as_str())
75:             .collect::<Vec<_>>()
76:             .join("\n");
77:         let tool_payload = slice.iter().rev().find_map(|t| t.tool_payload.clone());
78:         out.push(Chunk {
79:             chunk_id: format!("c{start}"),
80:             source_text,
81:             tool_payload,
82:             turn_indices: (start..end).collect(),
83:         });
84:         start = end;
85:     }
86:     out
87: }

1: # Coverage playbook (Agent Memoir)
2: 
3: **Audience:** agents and humans implementing phases under a **≥90% function + line (per file)** gate (`cargo llvm-cov` / `make coverage`).
4: 
5: **Why this file exists:** Phase 100020 burned ~15× the expected time chasing **region** coverage theater and flaky Postgres suites. The gate is now **lines + functions only**. Regions may still appear in reports; they are informational — **do not** invent unreachable `Err` arms to close them.
6: 
7: Also linked from `AGENTS.md` and `make help`.
8: 
9: ## Mistakes to not repeat
10: 
11: | Mistake | Better default |
12: |---------|----------------|
13: | Treat every `?` Err as must-hit for **region** % | Gate is lines + functions. Prefer `expect` / casts for infallible paths; inject failures only at real boundaries |
14: | Shared DB tests without a lock + poison recovery on the **test** lock | One `PG_TEST_LOCK` + `into_inner`; no destructive DDL on `public` |
15: | `into_inner` + `poison_*_for_test` on **production** mutexes | Production: `.lock().expect("… poisoned")`. No poison theater |
16: | Name test file `*_tests_extra.rs` | Name `*_tests.rs` / `*-tests.rs` / `tests.rs` so llvm-cov path-excludes it |
17: | Inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {…}` and assume it is excluded | **Not excluded.** Only path patterns above (and `tests/` dirs) are omitted by default |
18: | `reset_auto_extension` in parallel tests | Don’t mutate process-global SQLite state across threads |
19: | Finish code, then sync vocab docs | Same change: SQL + code + roadmap + glossary |
20: | Makefile `DATABASE_URL` DB name ≠ Compose `POSTGRES_DB` | One canonical DB (`clio`); keep Makefile, `.env.example`, test fallbacks, and this file identical |
21: | CI missing `--fail-under-functions` (or still requiring regions) | CI must match Makefile: **lines + functions** only — no `--fail-under-regions` |
22: | Fixed SQLite KNN over-fetch (`k*8`) then claim “exact” | Widen fetch until in-bank top-k is filled or exhausted; keep a multi-bank hostile test |
23: | Dead error mappers only unit-tested | Wire open/registration failures through the mapper (`Result`), or delete it |
24: | Run `make check` / coverage in a tight loop while fixing | One diagnostic run → wholesale fix → one verify run (laptop heat) |
25: | `make test` / `make check` without `--workspace` | Workspace has `default-members = [clio-lib]` — always pass `--workspace` or store tests never run |
26: | Drop a workspace.dependency while adding another | Keep `zerocopy` (etc.) when editing `Cargo.toml`; refresh `Cargo.lock` before `--locked` builds |
27: | Env fallback URL unhit under coverage (DATABASE_URL always set) | Extract `postgres_url_or_default(Result<…>)` and unit-test both Ok and Err arms |
28: | Fixed KNN `fetch_k = k.max(32)` never widens in tests | Start at `k.max(1)` so multi-bank cases must widen; keep a hostile foreign-neighbor test |
29: 
30: **Gate command (authoritative):**
31: 
32: ```bash
33: make coverage
34: # equivalent:
35: # cargo llvm-cov --workspace --locked --summary-only \
36: #   --fail-under-lines 90 --fail-under-functions 90
37: ```
38: 
39: `DATABASE_URL` defaults (via Makefile) to Compose Postgres:
40: 
41: `postgres://clio:clio@127.0.0.1:34310/clio`
42: 
43: **Per-file floor:** Humans lowered the lasting gate from 100% to **≥90% lines and functions on every reported source file** (not only the TOTAL row). `cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-*` enforces the aggregate floor; agents MUST still scan the per-file summary and stop if any file is under 90%.
44: 
45: All of `coverage`, `coverage-html`, `coverage-lcov`, and `coverage-open` MUST share that env. Do not special-case only `make coverage`. CI uses the same two `--fail-under-*` floors (port may differ for the Actions service).
46: 
47: `make check` = `fmt` + `clippy -D warnings` + `test` (not coverage). Still keep coverage green before claiming a phase done.
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 1. Order of operations (do this, in this order)
52: 
53: 1. **Baseline before edits.** Run `make coverage`. If any reported file is below **90%** lines or functions, **stop and raise**.
54: 2. **Implement behavior first.** Green `cargo test --locked` (and Clippy `-D warnings`) before hunting coverage misses.
55: 3. **Stabilize shared dependencies.** Postgres up (`make compose up …`), unique IDs, serialized access to shared DBs.
56: 4. **Then** run coverage. Fix real **line/function** misses with the decision tree in §3.
57: 5. **Do not** spend time closing region-only gaps. If a line is hit and the function runs, that is enough for the gate.
58: 
59: Do **not** open HTML / JSON coverage parsers until step 4.
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: ## 2. What the gate measures
64: 
65: | Metric | Gated? | Meaning in practice |
66: |--------|--------|---------------------|
67: | **Functions** | **Yes — ≥90% per file** | Every compiled function in reported crates was entered at least once. |
68: | **Lines** | **Yes — ≥90% per file** | Every instrumented line had ≥1 hit. |
69: | **Regions** | **No** | LLVM can split a line into multiple regions (`a()?.b()?`, `unwrap_or`). Unhit regions may still show in HTML/JSON — **ignore for the gate**. |
70: 
71: `cargo llvm-cov` HTML can paint a line green when any region on that line ran. For this repo, trust the **summary lines + functions** columns against the fail-under floors.
72: 
73: ### What llvm-cov reports (and ignores)
74: 
75: Per [cargo-llvm-cov README](https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov): by default the report **excludes** code under a directory named `tests` and files named `tests.rs`, `*_tests.rs`, or `*-tests.rs`.
76: 
77: - That exclusion is **path-based**, not “any `#[cfg(test)]` module.”
78: - Inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` inside a production `.rs` file **still counts** toward the gate (unless you use `#[coverage(off)]` on nightly).
79: - Names like `*_tests_extra.rs` are **not** excluded → they pollute the gate. Always use `*_tests.rs` for test-only modules (e.g. `assoc_edge_tests.rs`, `async_store_tests.rs`).
80: 
81: ### Diagnosing misses quickly
82: 
83: ```bash
84: export DATABASE_URL=postgres://clio:clio@127.0.0.1:34310/clio
85: cargo llvm-cov --workspace --locked --json --output-path /tmp/cov.json
86: # Inspect files with uncovered lines / functions (not region theater).
87: ```
88: 
89: Or: `make coverage-html` / `make coverage-open` once the suite is green.
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 3. Decision tree for an unhit **line** or **function**
94: 
95: Ask once, in order:
96: 
97: ### A. Is this code reachable in production?
98: 
99: | Kind | Examples | Action |
100: |------|----------|--------|
101: | **Infallible** | `serde_json::to_string` on a closed struct; ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypt; mutex poison after a bug | Use `.expect("…")` or a cast. Do not keep decorative `Result` arms. |
102: | **Trust boundary** | DB execute, connect, decrypt, sqlite-vec load | Keep `Result` + `?`. Prefer one shared mapper tested Ok + Err. |
103: | **Process-global / parallel-hostile** | `sqlite3_reset_auto_extension` | Fail closed via `Result` / `sqlite_vec_missing`; do not race other tests. |
104: | **Async join / spawn_blocking cancel** | `JoinError` | Prefer `.expect("store blocking task")` unless cancel is a product path. |
105: 
106: ### B. Matching the rest of this repo
107: 
108: Existing crates freely use `.expect(...)` on invariants. Do not burn hours on false arms.
109: 
110: ### C. After two failed attempts
111: 
112: Stop. Paste file + line, why it cannot be hit cheaply, and ask whether to delete or add one concrete test. Do not invent schema vandalism to close an arm — especially not for region-only gaps.
113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: ## 4. Patterns that burned Phase 100020 (anti-patterns)
117: 
118: ### 4.1 Dead `unwrap_or` / decorative `Result`
119: 
120: Prefer casts / `expect` for infallible paths. Saves line noise and avoids fake branches.
121: 
122: ### 4.2 Poison recovery vs poison theater
123: 
124: ```rust
125: // Test-only shared lock (PG_TEST_LOCK):
126: .lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
127:

# Coverage playbook (Agent Memoir)

**Audience:** agents and humans implementing phases under a **≥90% function + line (per file)** gate (`cargo llvm-cov` / `make coverage`).

**Why this file exists:** Phase 100020 burned ~15× the expected time chasing **region** coverage theater and flaky Postgres suites. The gate is now **lines + functions only**. Regions may still appear in reports; they are informational — **do not** invent unreachable `Err` arms to close them.

Also linked from `AGENTS.md` and `make help`.

## Mistakes to not repeat

| Mistake | Better default |
|---------|----------------|
| Treat every `?` Err as must-hit for **region** % | Gate is lines + functions. Prefer `expect` / casts for infallible paths; inject failures only at real boundaries |
| Shared DB tests without a lock + poison recovery on the **test** lock | One `PG_TEST_LOCK` + `into_inner`; no destructive DDL on `public` |
| `into_inner` + `poison_*_for_test` on **production** mutexes | Production: `.lock().expect("… poisoned")`. No poison theater |
| Name test file `*_tests_extra.rs` | Name `*_tests.rs` / `*-tests.rs` / `tests.rs` so llvm-cov path-excludes it |
| Inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {…}` and assume it is excluded | **Not excluded.** Only path patterns above (and `tests/` dirs) are omitted by default |
| `reset_auto_extension` in parallel tests | Don’t mutate process-global SQLite state across threads |
| Finish code, then sync vocab docs | Same change: SQL + code + roadmap + glossary |
| Makefile `DATABASE_URL` DB name ≠ Compose `POSTGRES_DB` | One canonical DB (`clio`); keep Makefile, `.env.example`, test fallbacks, and this file identical |
| CI missing `--fail-under-functions` (or still requiring regions) | CI must match Makefile: **lines + functions** only — no `--fail-under-regions` |
| Fixed SQLite KNN over-fetch (`k*8`) then claim “exact” | Widen fetch until in-bank top-k is filled or exhausted; keep a multi-bank hostile test |
| Dead error mappers only unit-tested | Wire open/registration failures through the mapper (`Result`), or delete it |
| Run `make check` / coverage in a tight loop while fixing | One diagnostic run → wholesale fix → one verify run (laptop heat) |
| `make test` / `make check` without `--workspace` | Workspace has `default-members = [clio-lib]` — always pass `--workspace` or store tests never run |
| Drop a workspace.dependency while adding another | Keep `zerocopy` (etc.) when editing `Cargo.toml`; refresh `Cargo.lock` before `--locked` builds |
| Env fallback URL unhit under coverage (DATABASE_URL always set) | Extract `postgres_url_or_default(Result<…>)` and unit-test both Ok and Err arms |
| Fixed KNN `fetch_k = k.max(32)` never widens in tests | Start at `k.max(1)` so multi-bank cases must widen; keep a hostile foreign-neighbor test |

**Gate command (authoritative):**

```bash
make coverage
# equivalent:
# cargo llvm-cov --workspace --locked --summary-only \
#   --fail-under-lines 90 --fail-under-functions 90
```

`DATABASE_URL` defaults (via Makefile) to Compose Postgres:

`postgres://clio:clio@127.0.0.1:34310/clio`

**Per-file floor:** Humans lowered the lasting gate from 100% to **≥90% lines and functions on every reported source file** (not only the TOTAL row). `cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-*` enforces the aggregate floor; agents MUST still scan the per-file summary and stop if any file is under 90%.

All of `coverage`, `coverage-html`, `coverage-lcov`, and `coverage-open` MUST share that env. Do not special-case only `make coverage`. CI uses the same two `--fail-under-*` floors (port may differ for the Actions service).

`make check` = `fmt` + `clippy -D warnings` + `test` (not coverage). Still keep coverage green before claiming a phase done.

---

## 1. Order of operations (do this, in this order)

1. **Baseline before edits.** Run `make coverage`. If any reported file is below **90%** lines or functions, **stop and raise**.
2. **Implement behavior first.** Green `cargo test --locked` (and Clippy `-D warnings`) before hunting coverage misses.
3. **Stabilize shared dependencies.** Postgres up (`make compose up …`), unique IDs, serialized access to shared DBs.
4. **Then** run coverage. Fix real **line/function** misses with the decision tree in §3.
5. **Do not** spend time closing region-only gaps. If a line is hit and the function runs, that is enough for the gate.

Do **not** open HTML / JSON coverage parsers until step 4.

---

## 2. What the gate measures

| Metric | Gated? | Meaning in practice |
|--------|--------|---------------------|
| **Functions** | **Yes — ≥90% per file** | Every compiled function in reported crates was entered at least once. |
| **Lines** | **Yes — ≥90% per file** | Every instrumented line had ≥1 hit. |
| **Regions** | **No** | LLVM can split a line into multiple regions (`a()?.b()?`, `unwrap_or`). Unhit regions may still show in HTML/JSON — **ignore for the gate**. |

`cargo llvm-cov` HTML can paint a line green when any region on that line ran. For this repo, trust the **summary lines + functions** columns against the fail-under floors.

### What llvm-cov reports (and ignores)

Per [cargo-llvm-cov README](https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov): by default the report **excludes** code under a directory named `tests` and files named `tests.rs`, `*_tests.rs`, or `*-tests.rs`.

- That exclusion is **path-based**, not “any `#[cfg(test)]` module.”
- Inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` inside a production `.rs` file **still counts** toward the gate (unless you use `#[coverage(off)]` on nightly).
- Names like `*_tests_extra.rs` are **not** excluded → they pollute the gate. Always use `*_tests.rs` for test-only modules (e.g. `assoc_edge_tests.rs`, `async_store_tests.rs`).

### Diagnosing misses quickly

```bash
export DATABASE_URL=postgres://clio:clio@127.0.0.1:34310/clio
cargo llvm-cov --workspace --locked --json --output-path /tmp/cov.json
# Inspect files with uncovered lines / functions (not region theater).
```

Or: `make coverage-html` / `make coverage-open` once the suite is green.

---

## 3. Decision tree for an unhit **line** or **function**

Ask once, in order:

### A. Is this code reachable in production?

| Kind | Examples | Action |
|------|----------|--------|
| **Infallible** | `serde_json::to_string` on a closed struct; ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypt; mutex poison after a bug | Use `.expect("…")` or a cast. Do not keep decorative `Result` arms. |
| **Trust boundary** | DB execute, connect, decrypt, sqlite-vec load | Keep `Result` + `?`. Prefer one shared mapper tested Ok + Err. |
| **Process-global / parallel-hostile** | `sqlite3_reset_auto_extension` | Fail closed via `Result` / `sqlite_vec_missing`; do not race other tests. |
| **Async join / spawn_blocking cancel** | `JoinError` | Prefer `.expect("store blocking task")` unless cancel is a product path. |

### B. Matching the rest of this repo

Existing crates freely use `.expect(...)` on invariants. Do not burn hours on false arms.

### C. After two failed attempts

Stop. Paste file + line, why it cannot be hit cheaply, and ask whether to delete or add one concrete test. Do not invent schema vandalism to close an arm — especially not for region-only gaps.

---

## 4. Patterns that burned Phase 100020 (anti-patterns)

### 4.1 Dead `unwrap_or` / decorative `Result`

Prefer casts / `expect` for infallible paths. Saves line noise and avoids fake branches.

### 4.2 Poison recovery vs poison theater

```rust
// Test-only shared lock (PG_TEST_LOCK):
.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())

// Production store / KMS mutexes:
.lock().expect("sqlite store mutex poisoned")
```

### 4.3 Counting every `.am("…")?` separately

Prefer one `IntoAmError` helper. One empty-schema failure often covers the driver-error path.

### 4.4 Shared Postgres without serialization

1. Serialize with `PG_TEST_LOCK` + `into_inner`.
2. Prefer private schemas.
3. Unique row IDs.

### 4.5 `DATABASE_URL` only on one Make target / wrong DB name

One Makefile `export DATABASE_URL ?= …/agentmemoir` for all coverage recipes; match `.env.example` and Compose.

### 4.6 Process-global SQLite extension reset

Do not call `reset_auto_extension` in tests. Registration/open failures go through `sqlite_vec_missing`.

### 4.7 SQLite bank-scoped KNN

Use widening fetch (`sqlite_knn::knn_in_bank`), not a fixed `k*8` cap. Keep a hostile multi-bank test.

### 4.8 Async adapter coverage

Put async adapter tests in `async_store_tests.rs` (path-excluded). Keep sync `Store` as the behavioral contract for most tests.

### 4.9 Renames without doc sync

Vocabulary renames require the same change for roadmap, glossary, `crates.md`, and comments.

### 4.10 Region hunting (retired)

Do **not** reintroduce `--fail-under-regions`. Unhit regions on an otherwise covered line are not a gate failure.

---

## 5. Design for coverage *while* implementing (not after)

1. **Small modules** (≤450 lines).
2. **One error sink** (`IntoAmError` / `sqlite_vec_missing`).
3. **Infallible crypto/serde/mutex poison:** `expect`.
4. **Test doubles at boundaries** (`FailEncryptKms`).
5. **Parity + `*_tests.rs` edge modules.**
6. **Name test modules `*_tests.rs`.**

---

## 6. Checklist before declaring a phase done

- [ ] `make coverage` exits 0 (**lines** and **functions** ≥90% aggregate); also confirm **each file** ≥90%.
- [ ] CI yaml matches: `--fail-under-lines 90` and `--fail-under-functions 90` only (no regions floor).
- [ ] `make coverage-html` / `coverage-open` green (same `DATABASE_URL`).
- [ ] `make check` clean with **`--workspace`** test/clippy scope (one verify run after a wholesale fix).
- [ ] `cargo test --locked` clean with `DATABASE_URL` unset (fallbacks → `clio`).
- [ ] Compose Postgres reachable when claiming Postgres parity.
- [ ] No `*_tests_extra.rs` production-reported test files.
- [ ] Phase exit / completion evidence filled when claiming phase done.
- [ ] Vocab renames reflected in docs if any occurred this phase.

---

## 7. Quick reference — commands

```bash
make compose up mac   # or: make compose up linux
make check            # fmt + clippy -D warnings + test
make coverage
make coverage-html
make coverage-open
```

Install if missing:

```bash
rustup component add llvm-tools-preview
cargo install cargo-llvm-cov
```

---

## 8. Phase 100020 postmortem (compressed)

| Symptom | Root cause | Fix that stuck |
|---------|------------|----------------|
| Hours on region % after lines green | Gate included regions | **Retired:** gate is lines + functions only |
| 22 pass / 9 fail on `coverage-open` | No `DATABASE_URL` on HTML + lock poison cascade | Shared Makefile export + test-lock `into_inner` |
| Suite flakes under llvm-cov | Parallel Postgres DDL on `public` | `PG_TEST_LOCK` + temp schemas |
| Coverage denominator spiked | `*_tests_extra.rs` counted | Rename to `*_tests.rs` |
| CI ≠ local functions gate | CI omitted `--fail-under-functions` | Align CI with Makefile |
| Fresh Compose vs Makefile DB | `am_store_test` not created by Compose | Standardize on `clio` |
| Bank KNN under-return | Fixed over-fetch | Widening `knn_in_bank` + hostile test |

**Time lesson:** stabilize tests first; cover lines/functions; never invent branches for region theater; one diagnostic run, wholesale fix, one verify.

---

## 9. Non-negotiables for future agents

1. Do not start a phase if any reported file is below **90%** line/function coverage — raise immediately.
2. Do not chase coverage before `cargo test` is green.
3. Do not invent unreachable `Err` arms or production poison helpers — especially not for regions.
4. Do not mutate process-global SQLite auto-extensions in parallel tests.
5. Do not leave coverage Make targets without the same env as the gate.
6. Do not reintroduce `--fail-under-regions` without an explicit human decision.
7. Keep CI `--fail-under-lines` / `--fail-under-functions` in lockstep with Makefile.
8. Keep `DATABASE_URL` DB name aligned with Compose / `.env.example`.

This file is normative for coverage work in this repo until superseded.

13: ## 1. Objective

15: ### Goal
16: Make new memory **queryable fast** (PR-9 / FR-3 / NFR-2): run **parallel chunk extraction**, **merge near-duplicates into a canonical unit**, and expose the **leaf immediately**. 20: - Each chunk uses Phase 100050 extract + span verify; failures follow FR-4 per chunk without failing unrelated chunks blindly (document partial-success policy).
21: - Near-duplicate candidates from parallel extraction consolidate into stable **canonical units** before they are treated as the durable leaf write unit.
22: - After canonical consolidation + gated admit, the new episodic item is **leaf-queryable** immediately—before any ancestor structural maintenance completes (FR-3).
23: - Target: newly written episodic item retrievable within a bounded window (NFR-2: under ~2 seconds of source turn completing), independent of background maintenance duration.
24: - `store` / ingest path returns success for leaf durability without waiting on MemTree summary refresh (slice 100070).
25: 
26: ### Parent Requirement
27: `requirement.md` (current) — P2, PR-9, §4.3 steps 1–2, FR-3, NFR-2; gated writes §4.9.3 / FR-21; fidelity via Phase 100050 / FR-4.
28: 
29: ### Design references (non-normative)
30: - Parallel chunk extraction + canonical fact consolidation before indexing: [MemForest](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.23986v2) (Chen et al., 2026) and [Concyclics/MemForest](https://github.com/Concyclics/MemForest).
31: - Canonicalization practice from MemForest: normalize surface forms → merge duplicates → keep non-equivalent updates as **separate temporally anchored facts** (do not overwrite older evidence during consolidation).
32: - Near-duplicate merge vs supersede distinction (merge equivalents only): related pattern discussion in [MemSIF](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.01742)—supersession of discrete facts remains slice 100080 / PR-6, not this consolidation step.
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## 2. Scope Boundaries
37: 
38: ### In Scope
39: - Session/turn partitioning into extraction chunks.
40: - Bounded-parallel invocation of Phase 100050 extraction + verification.
41: - Canonical consolidation: normalize + merge near-duplicate / equivalent candidates into one write unit; preserve provenance links to source chunks/spans.
42: - Leaf publish: after gated admission, mark item queryable at leaf level without waiting for ancestor refresh.
43: - Minimal leaf lookup path sufficient to prove FR-3 / NFR-2 (by id and/or simple time-ordered leaf list)—full hierarchical MemTree browse is slice 100070.
44: - Non-blocking handoff hook for dirty-path maintenance (slice 100070 can subscribe); MUST NOT require slice 100070 to complete for leaf reads.
45: 
46: ### Explicitly Out of Scope
47: - MemTree node hierarchy, dirty-path ancestor recompute, `maintenance_status` / `consolidate` tools (slice 100070).
48: - Bi-temporal triple supersession engine (slice 100080).
49: - Hub distillation / co-activation graph (slice 100130).
50: - Dense/lexical index rebuilds (slice 100110)—leaf queryability here is structural/id/time based, not hybrid retrieve.
51: - Offline RFT; MCP transports.
52: 
53: ### Must Not Change
54: - Phase 100050 span-verify rules and refuse-commit semantics.
55: - Phase 100040 admission gates on every long-term canonical write.
56: - Snapshot authoritative / gist non-authoritative (PR-4).
57: - PR-6: consolidation MUST NOT delete or silently overwrite a prior discrete fact under the guise of “merge” when the content is a contradictory update—contradictions become separate candidates / later triple supersession.

62: 2. Document the reason.
63: 3. Request clarification or approval.
64: 4. Do not silently expand scope.

88: where or how to implement the changes.

119: ## 5. Implementation Specification
120: 
121: ### Task 1: Chunk Partitioning and Bounded Parallel Extraction
122: 
123: #### Intent
124: Break the sequential extraction bottleneck (§4.3 step 1).
125: 
126: #### Required Capability or Behavior
127: - Partition a session/turn stream into chunks (document default size strategy; MemForest-style short multi-turn chunks are acceptable).
128: - Extract+verify chunks concurrently with a configurable concurrency limit `P`.
129: - Aggregate per-chunk results: verified candidates, verify-refused diagnostics, transport errors.
130: - Partial success policy (MUST document and test): e.g. verified chunks proceed to consolidation; failed chunks log and do not poison successful admits unless the caller requested all-or-nothing.
131: 
132: #### Architectural Responsibility
133: Write-path orchestrator / ingest pipeline.
134: 
135: #### Required Changes
136: 1. Chunker.
137: 2. Worker pool / async fan-out with hard concurrency cap.
138: 3. Structured aggregate result type.
139: 
140: #### Implementation Constraints
141: - Do not serialize all chunks through one LLM call “for simplicity” in the default path.
142: - Do not unbounded-spawn one task per token/turn without a cap.
143: - Each chunk still obeys Phase 100050 retry-once verify rules independently.
144: 
145: #### Expected Result
146: Tests show wall-clock overlap for multi-chunk fixtures with a fake extractor (concurrency probe), and correct aggregation.
147: 
148: ### Task 2: Canonical Near-Duplicate Consolidation
149: 
150: #### Intent
151: Repair fragmentation introduced by parallel extraction (§4.3 step 2).
152: 
153: #### Required Capability or Behavior
154: - Normalize surface forms (case/whitespace/Unicode policy documented).
155: - **Default merge path until slice 100110:** deterministic fingerprint / normalized exact match on key fields **only**. Embedding candidate search and LLM equivalence checks are **out of default production path** until dense index exists; if experimented with, they MUST NOT be the sole merge authority and MUST be behind an explicit config flag defaulting off.
156: - **Hard no-merge rule for discrete contradictions:** if two candidates share a normalized discrete key (`subject`+`predicate` when SPO-shaped, or an explicit discrete attribute key) and differ on object/value, they MUST NOT merge. Emit separate canonical units and/or hand off to `triple_add` supersession (Phase 100080). Never blend Boston/NYC-style updates into one value.
157: - Non-keyed near-duplicates (same fingerprint) merge with provenance union.
158: - Canonical unit retains provenance: source chunk ids, span evidence; confidence aggregation rule documented (e.g. max).
159: 
160: #### Architectural Responsibility
161: Canonicalization / fact-manager layer between extraction and gated write.
162: 
163: #### Required Changes
164: 1. Fingerprint / normalize helpers (deterministic-only default).
165: 2. Merge algorithm + **mandatory** discrete-key contradiction split.
166: 3. Provenance union on merged unit.
167: 4. Test: `lives_in` Boston vs NYC → two units / triple handoff, never one blended object.
168: 
169: #### Implementation Constraints
170: - Consolidation is **not** bi-temporal supersession (slice 100080) and **not** `discard`.
171: - Consolidation MUST NOT bypass Phase 100040 gates: the merged unit is still a candidate for admit.
172: - Do not merge across banks or actors.
173: - LLM/embedding merge MUST NOT be sole authority for keyed discrete attributes (even after slice 100110).
174: 
175: #### Expected Result
176: Two near-duplicate chunk outputs → one admitted leaf; contradictory objects for same subject+predicate → two candidates or explicit handoff note to triple path—not a blended value.
177: 
178: ### Task 3: Gated Admit of Canonical Leaf
179: 
180: #### Intent
181: Persist the canonical unit through existing gates with dual representation.
182: 
183: #### Required Capability or Behavior
184: - Run Phase 100040 gated write (and Phase 100050 verify if snapshot present / re-verify after merge if merge rewrote extractive fields).
185: - If merge rewrites snapshot text, re-run span verify against original sources before commit.
186: - On admit: repository create returns id; leaf marked queryable.
187: 
188: #### Architectural Responsibility
189: Application service using Phase 100030–005 stack.
190: 
191: #### Required Changes
192: 1. Post-merge verify-if-needed.
193: 2. Gated create for each surviving canonical unit.
194: 3. Telemetry: consolidate_merge counts, admit results.
195: 
196: #### Implementation Constraints
197: - No ungated repository create from the parallel path.
198: - Empty merged set → no write; log.
199: 
200: #### Expected Result
201: Integration: parallel extract → merge → single gated item with provenance.
202: 
203: ### Task 4: Immediate Leaf Queryability (Non-Blocking Maintenance)
204: 
205: #### Intent
206: Satisfy FR-3 / PR-9 / NFR-2: leaf readable before structural maintenance completes.
207: 
208: #### Required Capability or Behavior
209: - After Task 3 commit, `get` / leaf listing by id succeeds even if MemTree ancestors are dirty/absent.
210: - Emit a maintenance signal/event (“leaf attached / path dirty”) that slice 100070 can consume; if slice 100070 is not present yet, buffer or no-op without blocking.
211: - Ingest API MUST NOT await ancestor summary regeneration.
212: - **NFR-2 harness (required for exit):** with a **fixture/no-op extractor** (or recorded extract), measure wall-clock from ingest completion to successful leaf get; p95 MUST be **< 2 seconds** on the CI reference profile. Separately assert maintenance independence (slow fake consolidator does not block leaf get). Real LLM extract latency is reported as a distinct metric and MUST NOT be conflated with the NFR-2 leaf-publish budget (see `requirement.md` §8).
213: 
214: #### Architectural Responsibility
215: Leaf index / query façade + maintenance hook boundary + perf self-check.
216: 
217: #### Required Changes
218: 1. Explicit `leaf_queryable=true` (or equivalent) state on write completion.
219: 2. Read path that does not require clean ancestors.
220: 3. Async handoff stub for dirty-path refresh.
221: 4. Automated timing test for NFR-2 with fixture extractor.
222: 
223: #### Implementation Constraints
224: - Do not implement full MemTree refresh here.
225: - Do not block the write response on embedding rebuilds (slice 100110).
226: 
227: #### Expected Result
228: Test: write returns; immediate get-by-id succeeds; a simulated slow maintenance task started after write does not gate the read.

233: - The required behavior is satisfied.
234: - Architectural boundaries are respected.
235: - Existing contracts are preserved.

Make new memory **queryable fast** (PR-9 / FR-3 / NFR-2): run **parallel chunk extraction**, **merge near-duplicates into a canonical unit**, and expose the **leaf immediately**. Structural maintenance (MemTree ancestor refresh) MUST NOT block leaf readability—full tree maintenance lands in slice 100070; this slice owns §4.3 steps 1–2 and the leaf-queryability guarantee.

### Expected Outcome
- Incoming turns/sessions are partitioned into extraction chunks processed concurrently (bounded parallelism).
- Each chunk uses Phase 100050 extract + span verify; failures follow FR-4 per chunk without failing unrelated chunks blindly (document partial-success policy).
- Near-duplicate candidates from parallel extraction consolidate into stable **canonical units** before they are treated as the durable leaf write unit.
- After canonical consolidation + gated admit, the new episodic item is **leaf-queryable** immediately—before any ancestor structural maintenance completes (FR-3).
- Target: newly written episodic item retrievable within a bounded window (NFR-2: under ~2 seconds of source turn completing), independent of background maintenance duration.
- `store` / ingest path returns success for leaf durability without waiting on MemTree summary refresh (slice 100070).

### Parent Requirement
`requirement.md` (current) — P2, PR-9, §4.3 steps 1–2, FR-3, NFR-2; gated writes §4.9.3 / FR-21; fidelity via Phase 100050 / FR-4.

### Design references (non-normative)
- Parallel chunk extraction + canonical fact consolidation before indexing: [MemForest](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.23986v2) (Chen et al., 2026) and [Concyclics/MemForest](https://github.com/Concyclics/MemForest).
- Canonicalization practice from MemForest: normalize surface forms → merge duplicates → keep non-equivalent updates as **separate temporally anchored facts** (do not overwrite older evidence during consolidation).
- Near-duplicate merge vs supersede distinction (merge equivalents only): related pattern discussion in [MemSIF](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.01742)—supersession of discrete facts remains slice 100080 / PR-6, not this consolidation step.

---

## 2. Scope Boundaries

### In Scope
- Session/turn partitioning into extraction chunks.
- Bounded-parallel invocation of Phase 100050 extraction + verification.
- Canonical consolidation: normalize + merge near-duplicate / equivalent candidates into one write unit; preserve provenance links to source chunks/spans.
- Leaf publish: after gated admission, mark item queryable at leaf level without waiting for ancestor refresh.
- Minimal leaf lookup path sufficient to prove FR-3 / NFR-2 (by id and/or simple time-ordered leaf list)—full hierarchical MemTree browse is slice 100070.
- Non-blocking handoff hook for dirty-path maintenance (slice 100070 can subscribe); MUST NOT require slice 100070 to complete for leaf reads.

### Explicitly Out of Scope
- MemTree node hierarchy, dirty-path ancestor recompute, `maintenance_status` / `consolidate` tools (slice 100070).
- Bi-temporal triple supersession engine (slice 100080).
- Hub distillation / co-activation graph (slice 100130).
- Dense/lexical index rebuilds (slice 100110)—leaf queryability here is structural/id/time based, not hybrid retrieve.
- Offline RFT; MCP transports.

### Must Not Change
- Phase 100050 span-verify rules and refuse-commit semantics.
- Phase 100040 admission gates on every long-term canonical write.
- Snapshot authoritative / gist non-authoritative (PR-4).
- PR-6: consolidation MUST NOT delete or silently overwrite a prior discrete fact under the guise of “merge” when the content is a contradictory update—contradictions become separate candidates / later triple supersession.

### Scope Expansion Rule
If work outside this scope appears necessary:
1. Stop.
2. Document the reason.
3. Request clarification or approval.
4. Do not silently expand scope.

---

## 3. Preconditions and Dependencies

### Preconditions
- Phase 100050 accepted: extract + span verify + gated store wiring.
- Phase 100040 accepted: admission gates.
- Phase 100030 accepted: item repository.

### Dependencies
| Dependency | Required State | Validation |
|------------|----------------|------------|
| Extract+verify pipeline | Per-chunk callable | Phase 100050 tests |
| Gated write | Canonical unit admits only through gates | Phase 100040 tests |
| Async/concurrency primitive | Bounded parallel tasks | Runtime smoke |
| Leaf read API | Get-by-id (and/or leaf list) works post-write | Phase 100030 + this phase |

---

## 4. Existing-System Discovery

The agent MUST inspect the existing system before deciding
where or how to implement the changes.

### Required Discovery
- Identify the subsystem(s) responsible for the relevant behavior.
- Locate the existing implementation of related capabilities.
- Identify existing interfaces, contracts, schemas, and boundaries.
- Identify relevant tests and verification mechanisms.

from the actual repository. The plan does not prescribe file paths,
class names, module names, or directory structures unless they
are explicitly part of an externally required contract.

---

## 5. Implementation Specification

### Task 1: Chunk Partitioning and Bounded Parallel Extraction

#### Intent
Break the sequential extraction bottleneck (§4.3 step 1).

#### Required Capability or Behavior
- Partition a session/turn stream into chunks (document default size strategy; MemForest-style short multi-turn chunks are acceptable).
- Extract+verify chunks concurrently with a configurable concurrency limit `P`.
- Aggregate per-chunk results: verified candidates, verify-refused diagnostics, transport errors.
- Partial success policy (MUST document and test): e.g. verified chunks proceed to consolidation; failed chunks log and do not poison successful admits unless the caller requested all-or-nothing.

#### Architectural Responsibility
Write-path orchestrator / ingest pipeline.

#### Required Changes
1. Chunker.
2. Worker pool / async fan-out with hard concurrency cap.
3. Structured aggregate result type.

#### Implementation Constraints
- Do not serialize all chunks through one LLM call “for simplicity” in the default path.
- Do not unbounded-spawn one task per token/turn without a cap.
- Each chunk still obeys Phase 100050 retry-once verify rules independently.

#### Expected Result
Tests show wall-clock overlap for multi-chunk fixtures with a fake extractor (concurrency probe), and correct aggregation.

### Task 2: Canonical Near-Duplicate Consolidation

#### Intent
Repair fragmentation introduced by parallel extraction (§4.3 step 2).

#### Required Capability or Behavior
- Normalize surface forms (case/whitespace/Unicode policy documented).
- **Default merge path until slice 100110:** deterministic fingerprint / normalized exact match on key fields **only**. Embedding candidate search and LLM equivalence checks are **out of default production path** until dense index exists; if experimented with, they MUST NOT be the sole merge authority and MUST be behind an explicit config flag defaulting off.
- **Hard no-merge rule for discrete contradictions:** if two candidates share a normalized discrete key (`subject`+`predicate` when SPO-shaped, or an explicit discrete attribute key) and differ on object/value, they MUST NOT merge. Emit separate canonical units and/or hand off to `triple_add` supersession (Phase 100080). Never blend Boston/NYC-style updates into one value.
- Non-keyed near-duplicates (same fingerprint) merge with provenance union.
- Canonical unit retains provenance: source chunk ids, span evidence; confidence aggregation rule documented (e.g. max).

#### Architectural Responsibility
Canonicalization / fact-manager layer between extraction and gated write.

#### Required Changes
1. Fingerprint / normalize helpers (deterministic-only default).
2. Merge algorithm + **mandatory** discrete-key contradiction split.
3. Provenance union on merged unit.
4. Test: `lives_in` Boston vs NYC → two units / triple handoff, never one blended object.

#### Implementation Constraints
- Consolidation is **not** bi-temporal supersession (slice 100080) and **not** `discard`.
- Consolidation MUST NOT bypass Phase 100040 gates: the merged unit is still a candidate for admit.
- Do not merge across banks or actors.
- LLM/embedding merge MUST NOT be sole authority for keyed discrete attributes (even after slice 100110).

#### Expected Result
Two near-duplicate chunk outputs → one admitted leaf; contradictory objects for same subject+predicate → two candidates or explicit handoff note to triple path—not a blended value.

### Task 3: Gated Admit of Canonical Leaf

#### Intent
Persist the canonical unit through existing gates with dual representation.

#### Required Capability or Behavior
- Run Phase 100040 gated write (and Phase 100050 verify if snapshot present / re-verify after merge if merge rewrote extractive fields).
- If merge rewrites snapshot text, re-run span verify against original sources before commit.
- On admit: repository create returns id; leaf marked queryable.

#### Architectural Responsibility
Application service using Phase 100030–005 stack.

#### Required Changes
1. Post-merge verify-if-needed.
2. Gated create for each surviving canonical unit.
3. Telemetry: consolidate_merge counts, admit results.

#### Implementation Constraints
- No ungated repository create from the parallel path.
- Empty merged set → no write; log.

#### Expected Result
Integration: parallel extract → merge → single gated item with provenance.

### Task 4: Immediate Leaf Queryability (Non-Blocking Maintenance)

#### Intent
Satisfy FR-3 / PR-9 / NFR-2: leaf readable before structural maintenance completes.

#### Required Capability or Behavior
- After Task 3 commit, `get` / leaf listing by id succeeds even if MemTree ancestors are dirty/absent.
- Emit a maintenance signal/event (“leaf attached / path dirty”) that slice 100070 can consume; if slice 100070 is not present yet, buffer or no-op without blocking.
- Ingest API MUST NOT await ancestor summary regeneration.
- **NFR-2 harness (required for exit):** with a **fixture/no-op extractor** (or recorded extract), measure wall-clock from ingest completion to successful leaf get; p95 MUST be **< 2 seconds** on the CI reference profile. Separately assert maintenance independence (slow fake consolidator does not block leaf get). Real LLM extract latency is reported as a distinct metric and MUST NOT be conflated with the NFR-2 leaf-publish budget (see `requirement.md` §8).

#### Architectural Responsibility
Leaf index / query façade + maintenance hook boundary + perf self-check.

#### Required Changes
1. Explicit `leaf_queryable=true` (or equivalent) state on write completion.
2. Read path that does not require clean ancestors.
3. Async handoff stub for dirty-path refresh.
4. Automated timing test for NFR-2 with fixture extractor.

#### Implementation Constraints
- Do not implement full MemTree refresh here.
- Do not block the write response on embedding rebuilds (slice 100110).

#### Expected Result
Test: write returns; immediate get-by-id succeeds; a simulated slow maintenance task started after write does not gate the read.

### Implementation Freedom
The agent may choose the concrete implementation structure,
file locations, naming, and internal design provided that:
- The required behavior is satisfied.
- Architectural boundaries are respected.
- Existing contracts are preserved.
- All acceptance criteria pass.
- No prohibited changes are introduced.

## 7. Security Constraints

### Required Controls

- Admission and span verify remain mandatory on canonical units.

- Never commit secrets.
- Use approved configuration for extractor endpoints.

- Partial batch cannot admit into the wrong bank.

- [x] Integration tests

| AC ID | Acceptance Criterion | Verification Method | Required Evidence |

| AC-100060-01 | Parallel chunk extraction with bounded concurrency | T100060-01 | `cargo test -p clio-write` — `t01_chunks_run_concurrently_under_cap` PASS (wall-clock overlap under P=4) |

### Expected Failure Modes

|---------|-----------|----------|
| Worker timeout | Future/join error | Mark chunk failed; continue per partial policy |
| Merge ambiguity | Conflicting equivalence | Keep separate; log; do not invent blended fact |
| Admit reject after merge | Gate/verify | No leaf; log factors/verify reasons |
| Maintenance hook flood | Queue depth | Coalesce signals (slice 100070 will coalesce dirty marks); never block leaf write |

### Rollback Strategy
Feature-flag parallel ingest off → fall back to single-chunk Phase 100050→004 path. Leaves already admitted remain. No need to unwind MemTree (not required yet).

If only part of the phase is complete:
- Do not claim full completion.
- Record completed and incomplete work separately.
- Document remaining work.
- Do not leave undocumented broken state.

122: ///
123: /// # Errors
124: /// Missing `source_text` when snapshot present; structural / signal errors.
125: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
126: pub fn admit_preview_verified(
127:     item: &mut MemoryItem,
128:     ctx: &OpContext,
129:     source_text: Option<&str>,
130:     evidence_ref: Option<&str>,
131:     fields: &[FieldSpec],

136:     verify_sink: &dyn VerifySink,

138: ) -> Result<Decision, AmError> {
139:     apply_evidence_ref(item, evidence_ref);
140:     item.validate()?;
141:     if let Some(text) = require_source_text(item, source_text)? {
142:         let report = verify_snapshot(
143:             text,

146:             verify,
147:         );
148:         if !report.ok {

150:             return Ok(verify_reject(&report));
151:         }
152:         emit_verify(verify_sink, "verify_ok", item, ctx, timestamp, &report);
153:     }
154:     let signals = signals_for(item, source)?;
155:     admit_preview(candidate, &signals, policy)
156: }

162: pub fn gated_store_verified(
163:     req: &mut VerifiedStoreRequest<'_>,

165:     source: &dyn SignalSource,
166:     write: &mut dyn FnMut(&MemoryItem) -> Result<(), AmError>,
167: ) -> Result<Decision, AmError> {

172:     req.item.validate()?;
173:     if let Some(text) = require_source_text(&req.item, req.source_text)? {
174:         let report = verify_snapshot(
175:             text,

177:             req.fields,
178:             &req.verify,
179:         );
180:         if !report.ok {

182:                 req.verify_sink,
183:                 "verify_fail",
184:                 &req.item,
185:                 req.ctx,
186:                 req.timestamp,
187:                 &report,
188:             );
189:             let decision = verify_reject(&report);
190:             req.admit_sink.emit(AdmissionEvent {
191:                 operation: "admit_reject".into(),
192:                 candidate_key: candidate.key().into(),
193:                 candidate_kind: candidate.kind().as_str().into(),
194:                 admission_score: Some(0.0),
195:                 rejection_reason: decision.rejection_reason.clone(),
196:                 bank: req.ctx.bank.as_str().into(),

198:                 timestamp: req.timestamp.into(),
199:                 preview: redact_preview(req.item.snapshot.as_ref(), req.item.gist.as_deref(), None),
200:             });

202:         }
203:         emit_verify(
204:             req.verify_sink,
205:             "verify_ok",
206:             &req.item,
207:             req.ctx,
208:             req.timestamp,
209:             &report,
210:         );
211:     }
212:     let gate = GateRequest {
213:         item: &req.item,
214:         ctx: req.ctx,
215:         policy: req.policy,
216:         sink: req.admit_sink,
217:         timestamp: req.timestamp,
218:     };

1: # Agent Memoir — Hardware & Deployment Profiles
2: 
3: **Document status:** Planning · **Version:** 1.3 · **Companion to:** `requirement.md` v1.6
4: 
5: This document defines three supported deployment profiles for the Agent Memoir Rust CLI. Profiles differ by what runs locally versus via API. Behavioral requirements in `requirement.md` are identical across profiles; only the inference and storage placement changes.
6: 
7: **Normative language:** MUST / SHOULD / MAY follow the same conventions as `requirement.md`.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## Shared assumptions (all profiles)
12: 
13: | Component | Placement |
14: |---|---|
15: | Agent Memoir CLI | Source in this repo (Rust binary you build); not a Compose service |
16: | Persistence | **PostgreSQL with `pgvector`** (Compose sidecar by default; external Postgres MAY be used) |
17: | SQLite | Supported as a zero-Docker alternative; not the Compose default |
18: | Embed / rerank / extract | Compose sidecars only when the profile includes them — **not** host-installed model servers |
19: 
20: The CLI talks to embed, rerank, and LLM endpoints through configurable base URLs. Switching a profile is configuration only; it MUST NOT fork product behavior.
21: 
22: **Compose default data plane:** when `docker compose up -d` is used, prefer **pgvector in Docker**, not SQLite.
23: 
24: ---
25: 
26: ## Profile A — CLI + local pgvector + API inference
27: 
28: **Name:** `api-inference`  
29: **Target:** any machine that can run Docker (or an external Postgres) and reach LLM / embed / rerank APIs.
30: 
31: ### Runs locally
32: 
33: | Service | Notes |
34: |---|---|
35: | Agent Memoir CLI | Rust binary |
36: | PostgreSQL + `pgvector` | Compose sidecar or external managed Postgres |
37: 
38: ### Runs via API keys
39: 
40: | Capability | Notes |
41: |---|---|
42: | LLM (extraction, gist, failure lessons, host agent) | Provider API (OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / compatible) |
43: | Embeddings | Provider embedding API |
44: | Reranker | Provider rerank API (or omit if hybrid retrieve uses dense+lexical only) |
45: 
46: ### Minimum hardware
47: 
48: | Resource | Guidance |
49: |---|---|
50: | vCPU | 1+ |
51: | RAM | 2 GB+ free for CLI + slim Postgres (`shared_buffers` capped) |
52: | Disk | Postgres volume + binary |
53: 
54: ### When to use
55: 
56: - Lowest local footprint
57: - Best extraction / answer quality (frontier APIs)
58: - Laptops and CI that should not load ONNX models
59: 
60: ### Compose sketch
61: 
62: ```text
63: services: postgres (pgvector)
64: env: DATABASE_URL, LLM_API_*, EMBED_API_*, RERANK_API_*
65: ```
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## Profile B — Local retrieve stack + API LLM
70: 
71: **Name:** `local-retrieval`  
72: **Target:** **2 vCPU · 8 GB RAM** (or better).
73: 
74: ### Runs locally
75: 
76: | Service | Model / image | Approx. RAM |
77: |---|---|---|
78: | Agent Memoir CLI | Rust binary | ~0.2–0.4 GB |
79: | PostgreSQL + `pgvector` | slim Compose Postgres | ~0.2–0.4 GB (capped) |
80: | Embedder | `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` · **dim 384** | ~0.25–0.3 GB |
81: | Reranker | `Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-reranker-base` (~306M); Compose TEI serves **`onnx-community/gte-multilingual-reranker-base`** (same model + ONNX for TEI CPU/ORT) | ~0.6–0.9 GB |
82: 
83: ### Runs via API keys
84: 
85: | Capability | Notes |
86: |---|---|
87: | LLM | Required — extraction, gist, lessons, host agent stay on provider APIs |
88: 
89: ### Hardware budget (2 vCPU · 8 GB)
90: 
91: | Piece | Approx. |
92: |---|---|
93: | OS + Docker | ~1–1.5 GB |
94: | CLI + pgvector + embed + rerank | ~1.5–2.5 GB |
95: | Headroom | ~3–4 GB |
96: 
97: **2 vCPU note:** embed and rerank share cores. Cap rerank candidates (e.g. top 30–50) and token lengths so p95 stays acceptable. Compose MUST set TEI `--max-batch-tokens` well below the default `16384` (we use `2048`) or CPU ORT warmup OOMs — see TEI issues #819 / #280.
98: 
99: ### When to use
100: 
101: - Offline or private retrieval / ranking
102: - Still want frontier LLM quality for extraction and answers
103: - Default recommended laptop profile for coding agents
104: 
105: ### Compose sketch
106: 
107: ```text
108: services: postgres (pgvector), embed (bge-small-en-v1.5), rerank (gte-multilingual-reranker-base)
109: env: DATABASE_URL, EMBED_URL, RERANK_URL, LLM_API_*
110: ```
111: 
112: ---
113: 
114: ## Profile C — Local retrieve stack + local NuExtract extractor
115: 
116: **Name:** `local-rft`  
117: **Target:** **4 vCPU · 12 GB RAM** (or better).
118: 
119: ### Runs locally
120: 
121: | Service | Model / image | Approx. RAM |
122: |---|---|---|
123: | Agent Memoir CLI | Rust binary | ~0.2–0.4 GB |
124: | PostgreSQL + `pgvector` | slim Compose Postgres | ~0.2–0.4 GB (capped) |
125: | Embedder | `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` · **dim 384** | ~0.25–0.3 GB |
126: | Reranker | `Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-reranker-base` (~306M); Compose TEI serves **`onnx-community/gte-multilingual-reranker-base`** (same model + ONNX for TEI CPU/ORT) | ~0.6–0.9 GB |
127: | Local extractor | **`numind/NuExtract-1.5-tiny`** (Qwen2.5-0.5B fine-tune for template→JSON extraction) | **~0.6–1.0 GB** (Q4_K_M GGUF ≈ 0.3 GB on disk) |
128: 
129: ### Optional via API keys
130: 
131: | Capability | Notes |
132: |---|---|
133: | Host companion / coding agent LLM | MAY remain on API for answer quality while extraction stays local |
134: | Fallback extractor | MAY fall back to API if local extract fails verification twice (`requirement.md` FR-4) |
135: 
136: ### Hardware budget (4 vCPU · 12 GB)
137: 
138: | Piece | Approx. |
139: |---|---|
140: | OS + Docker | ~1–1.5 GB |
141: | CLI + pgvector + embed + rerank | ~1.5–2.5 GB |
142: | `NuExtract-1.5-tiny` | ~0.6–1.0 GB |
143: | Headroom | **~6–8 GB** |
144: 
145: **4 vCPU note:** pin extractor threads (e.g. leave 1 core free for Postgres/embed) so the host stays responsive. Keep context short (e.g. 2k–4k). Structural maintenance stays background (PR-9).
146: 
147: ### Extractor constraints (normative intent)
148: 
149: - **Default local extractor is `numind/NuExtract-1.5-tiny`.** Runs as the Compose `extract` service (`ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server` + GGUF Q4_K_M in `./models/`). Use **temperature ≈ 0**. Pass a JSON **template** describing the snapshot schema; NuExtract is trained for template-guided extraction with span-faithful bias. Do **not** run a separate host-side Ollama/llama.cpp for this role.
150: - Online write path MUST still run the **cheap span verifier** (`requirement.md` §4.4 / FR-4). Unverified snapshots MUST NOT commit.
151: - Optional later: further offline RFT/LoRA on this base (or a successor) for Agent Memoir schemas; full rejection-sampling MUST NOT run per live request (§2.6).
152: - Larger local LLMs (1.5B–3B+) MAY be used for experiments but are **not** the Profile C default. 7B+ co-resident with embed + rerank + Postgres is out of scope for the 12 GB default.
153: 
154: ### When to use
155: 
156: - Air-gapped or low-egress environments for memory writes
157: - Lower per-token cost on high write volume
158: - Comfortable RAM headroom on 12 GB while keeping retrieval fully local
159: 
160: ### Compose sketch
161: 
162: ```text
163: services: postgres (pgvector), embed (bge-small-en-v1.5), rerank (gte-multilingual-reranker-base), extract (NuExtract-1.5-tiny via Compose llama.cpp server)
164: profiles: local-rft
165: env: DATABASE_URL, EMBED_URL, RERANK_URL, EXTRACT_URL (Compose NuExtract), optional LLM_API_* for host-agent / fallback
166: ```
167: 
168: ---
169: 
170: ## Profile comparison
171: 
172: | | **A · api-inference** | **B · local-retrieval** | **C · local-rft** |
173: |---|---|---|---|
174: | Min CPU / RAM | 1 vCPU / 2 GB+ | **2 vCPU / 8 GB** | **4 vCPU / 12 GB** |
175: | pgvector | Local (Compose) | Local (Compose) | Local (Compose) |
176: | Embed | API | `bge-small-en-v1.5` (384d) | `bge-small-en-v1.5` (384d) |
177: | Rerank | API (optional) | `gte-multilingual-reranker-base` | `gte-multilingual-reranker-base` |
178: | LLM / extractor | API | API | **`numind/NuExtract-1.5-tiny`** (API optional fallback) |
179: | Best for | Quality, simplicity | Private retrieve + cloud LLM | Private write path |
180: 
181: ---
182: 
183: ## Non-goals for these profiles
184: 
185: - Shipping a frontier-class local LLM as the default answer model on 8–12 GB
186: - Co-running `bge-reranker-v2-m3` FP16 plus a 7B LLM on the same 12 GB host as the default
187: - Using LightMem’s `Llama-3.2-1B` as the default snapshot extractor (different role: control-plane rewrite/write, not span-verified JSON extract)
188: - Requiring GPU; all three profiles are **CPU-first** (GPU MAY accelerate Profile C)
189: 
190: ---
191: 
192: ## Related documents
193: 
194: - `requirement.md` — behavior, tool catalog, backends (Postgres/`pgvector` and SQLite)
195: - `compose.yml` — sidecars for profiles below; SQL in `schema/`
196: - `.env.example` — `DATABASE_URL` / `EMBED_URL` / `RERANK_URL` / `EXTRACT_URL`
197:
