# Agent Memoir — Hardware & Deployment Profiles

**Document status:** Planning · **Version:** 1.3 · **Companion to:** `requirement.md` v1.6

This document defines three supported deployment profiles for the Agent Memoir Rust CLI. Profiles differ by what runs locally versus via API. Behavioral requirements in `requirement.md` are identical across profiles; only the inference and storage placement changes.

**Normative language:** MUST / SHOULD / MAY follow the same conventions as `requirement.md`.

---

## Shared assumptions (all profiles)

| Component | Placement |
|---|---|
| Agent Memoir CLI | Source in this repo (Rust binary you build); not a Compose service |
| Persistence | **PostgreSQL with `pgvector`** (Compose sidecar by default; external Postgres MAY be used) |
| SQLite | Supported as a zero-Docker alternative; not the Compose default |
| Embed / rerank / extract | Compose sidecars only when the profile includes them — **not** host-installed model servers |

The CLI talks to embed, rerank, and LLM endpoints through configurable base URLs. Switching a profile is configuration only; it MUST NOT fork product behavior.

**Compose default data plane:** when `docker compose up -d` is used, prefer **pgvector in Docker**, not SQLite.

---

## Profile A — CLI + local pgvector + API inference

**Name:** `api-inference`  
**Target:** any machine that can run Docker (or an external Postgres) and reach LLM / embed / rerank APIs.

### Runs locally

| Service | Notes |
|---|---|
| Agent Memoir CLI | Rust binary |
| PostgreSQL + `pgvector` | Compose sidecar or external managed Postgres |

### Runs via API keys

| Capability | Notes |
|---|---|
| LLM (extraction, gist, failure lessons, host agent) | Provider API (OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / compatible) |
| Embeddings | Provider embedding API |
| Reranker | Provider rerank API (or omit if hybrid retrieve uses dense+lexical only) |

### Minimum hardware

| Resource | Guidance |
|---|---|
| vCPU | 1+ |
| RAM | 2 GB+ free for CLI + slim Postgres (`shared_buffers` capped) |
| Disk | Postgres volume + binary |

### When to use

- Lowest local footprint
- Best extraction / answer quality (frontier APIs)
- Laptops and CI that should not load ONNX models

### Compose sketch

```text
services: postgres (pgvector)
env: DATABASE_URL, LLM_API_*, EMBED_API_*, RERANK_API_*
```

---

## Profile B — Local retrieve stack + API LLM

**Name:** `local-retrieval`  
**Target:** **2 vCPU · 8 GB RAM** (or better).

### Runs locally

| Service | Model / image | Approx. RAM |
|---|---|---|
| Agent Memoir CLI | Rust binary | ~0.2–0.4 GB |
| PostgreSQL + `pgvector` | slim Compose Postgres | ~0.2–0.4 GB (capped) |
| Embedder | `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` · **dim 384** | ~0.25–0.3 GB |
| Reranker | `Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-reranker-base` (~306M); Compose TEI serves **`onnx-community/gte-multilingual-reranker-base`** (same model + ONNX for TEI CPU/ORT) | ~0.6–0.9 GB |

### Runs via API keys

| Capability | Notes |
|---|---|
| LLM | Required — extraction, gist, lessons, host agent stay on provider APIs |

### Hardware budget (2 vCPU · 8 GB)

| Piece | Approx. |
|---|---|
| OS + Docker | ~1–1.5 GB |
| CLI + pgvector + embed + rerank | ~1.5–2.5 GB |
| Headroom | ~3–4 GB |

**2 vCPU note:** embed and rerank share cores. Cap rerank candidates (e.g. top 30–50) and token lengths so p95 stays acceptable. Compose MUST set TEI `--max-batch-tokens` well below the default `16384` (we use `2048`) or CPU ORT warmup OOMs — see TEI issues #819 / #280.

### When to use

- Offline or private retrieval / ranking
- Still want frontier LLM quality for extraction and answers
- Default recommended laptop profile for coding agents

### Compose sketch

```text
services: postgres (pgvector), embed (bge-small-en-v1.5), rerank (gte-multilingual-reranker-base)
env: DATABASE_URL, EMBED_URL, RERANK_URL, LLM_API_*
```

---

## Profile C — Local retrieve stack + local NuExtract extractor

**Name:** `local-rft`  
**Target:** **4 vCPU · 12 GB RAM** (or better).

### Runs locally

| Service | Model / image | Approx. RAM |
|---|---|---|
| Agent Memoir CLI | Rust binary | ~0.2–0.4 GB |
| PostgreSQL + `pgvector` | slim Compose Postgres | ~0.2–0.4 GB (capped) |
| Embedder | `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` · **dim 384** | ~0.25–0.3 GB |
| Reranker | `Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-reranker-base` (~306M); Compose TEI serves **`onnx-community/gte-multilingual-reranker-base`** (same model + ONNX for TEI CPU/ORT) | ~0.6–0.9 GB |
| Local extractor | **`numind/NuExtract-1.5-tiny`** (Qwen2.5-0.5B fine-tune for template→JSON extraction) | **~0.6–1.0 GB** (Q4_K_M GGUF ≈ 0.3 GB on disk) |

### Optional via API keys

| Capability | Notes |
|---|---|
| Host companion / coding agent LLM | MAY remain on API for answer quality while extraction stays local |
| Fallback extractor | MAY fall back to API if local extract fails verification twice (`requirement.md` FR-4) |

### Hardware budget (4 vCPU · 12 GB)

| Piece | Approx. |
|---|---|
| OS + Docker | ~1–1.5 GB |
| CLI + pgvector + embed + rerank | ~1.5–2.5 GB |
| `NuExtract-1.5-tiny` | ~0.6–1.0 GB |
| Headroom | **~6–8 GB** |

**4 vCPU note:** pin extractor threads (e.g. leave 1 core free for Postgres/embed) so the host stays responsive. Keep context short (e.g. 2k–4k). Structural maintenance stays background (PR-9).

### Extractor constraints (normative intent)

- **Default local extractor is `numind/NuExtract-1.5-tiny`.** Runs as the Compose `extract` service (`ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server` + GGUF Q4_K_M in `./models/`). Use **temperature ≈ 0**. Pass a JSON **template** describing the snapshot schema; NuExtract is trained for template-guided extraction with span-faithful bias. Do **not** run a separate host-side Ollama/llama.cpp for this role.
- Online write path MUST still run the **cheap span verifier** (`requirement.md` §4.4 / FR-4). Unverified snapshots MUST NOT commit.
- Optional later: further offline RFT/LoRA on this base (or a successor) for Agent Memoir schemas; full rejection-sampling MUST NOT run per live request (§2.6).
- Larger local LLMs (1.5B–3B+) MAY be used for experiments but are **not** the Profile C default. 7B+ co-resident with embed + rerank + Postgres is out of scope for the 12 GB default.

### When to use

- Air-gapped or low-egress environments for memory writes
- Lower per-token cost on high write volume
- Comfortable RAM headroom on 12 GB while keeping retrieval fully local

### Compose sketch

```text
services: postgres (pgvector), embed (bge-small-en-v1.5), rerank (gte-multilingual-reranker-base), extract (NuExtract-1.5-tiny via Compose llama.cpp server)
profiles: local-rft
env: DATABASE_URL, EMBED_URL, RERANK_URL, EXTRACT_URL (Compose NuExtract), optional LLM_API_* for host-agent / fallback
```

---

## Profile comparison

| | **A · api-inference** | **B · local-retrieval** | **C · local-rft** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Min CPU / RAM | 1 vCPU / 2 GB+ | **2 vCPU / 8 GB** | **4 vCPU / 12 GB** |
| pgvector | Local (Compose) | Local (Compose) | Local (Compose) |
| Embed | API | `bge-small-en-v1.5` (384d) | `bge-small-en-v1.5` (384d) |
| Rerank | API (optional) | `gte-multilingual-reranker-base` | `gte-multilingual-reranker-base` |
| LLM / extractor | API | API | **`numind/NuExtract-1.5-tiny`** (API optional fallback) |
| Best for | Quality, simplicity | Private retrieve + cloud LLM | Private write path |

---

## Non-goals for these profiles

- Shipping a frontier-class local LLM as the default answer model on 8–12 GB
- Co-running `bge-reranker-v2-m3` FP16 plus a 7B LLM on the same 12 GB host as the default
- Using LightMem’s `Llama-3.2-1B` as the default snapshot extractor (different role: control-plane rewrite/write, not span-verified JSON extract)
- Requiring GPU; all three profiles are **CPU-first** (GPU MAY accelerate Profile C)

---

## Related documents

- `requirement.md` — behavior, tool catalog, backends (Postgres/`pgvector` and SQLite)
- `compose.yml` — sidecars for profiles below; SQL in `schema/`
- `.env.example` — `DATABASE_URL` / `EMBED_URL` / `RERANK_URL` / `EXTRACT_URL`

### Compose commands

Prefer Make (arch is a flag; default profile is `local-rft`):

```bash
make compose up mac      # arm64 → compose.arm64.yml
make compose up linux    # amd64 → compose.amd64.yml
```

Override profile: `make compose up mac PROFILE=local-retrieval` or `PROFILE=` (postgres only).

Or call Compose directly — always pass an arch file (`-f compose.amd64.yml` or `-f compose.arm64.yml`). TEI CPU images differ by architecture; `llama.cpp:server` is multi-arch but is platform-pinned the same way.

| Profile | amd64 | arm64 |
|---|---|---|
| A · `api-inference` | `docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.amd64.yml up -d` | `docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.arm64.yml up -d` |
| B · `local-retrieval` | `docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.amd64.yml --profile local-retrieval up -d` | `docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.arm64.yml --profile local-retrieval up -d` |
| C · `local-rft` | `docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.amd64.yml --profile local-rft up -d` | `docker compose -f compose.yml -f compose.arm64.yml --profile local-rft up -d` |

Profile C also needs `./models/NuExtract-tiny-v1.5-Q4_K_M.gguf` before `extract` will stay healthy.

Schema: `schema/001_core.sql` is portable. Compose applies `002_vectors_postgres.sql` on first Postgres init. SQLite path: apply `001_core.sql` then `002_vectors_sqlite.sql`.

**Document status:** Planning · **Version:** 1.3

---

*End of document.*

1: // Copyright 2026 Agent Memoir Developers (https://agentmemoir.com/)

3: //
4: //
5: //! # Responsibility
6: //!
7: //! This module is responsible for the gated public write wrapper and reject telemetry.
8: //!
9: //! ## Owns
10: //! - `GateRequest`, `gated_create`, and raw-discriminator `gated_create_raw`
11: //! - Accept/reject events with secret-masked previews
12: //!
13: //! ## Does not own
14: //! - Scoring decisions (see `decision`)
15: //! - Durable storage drivers
16: //!
17: //! ## Boundary
18: //!
19: //! Changes to write wiring or event shape should normally require changes here.
20: //! Changes to scoring math should not require changes here.
21: //!
22: //! Keep this module focused on gated writes and telemetry.
23: 
24: use crate::decision::{Candidate, Decision, SignalInputs, decide, gate_reject};
25: use crate::policy::AdmissionPolicy;
26: use clio_config::secret::{masked_clone, scrub_inline_secrets};
27: use clio_types::{AmError, EpisodicType, ErrorCode, MemoryItem, OpContext, SemanticCategory};
28: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
29: use serde_json::Value;
30: use std::sync::Mutex;
31: 
32: /// Durable-shaped admit/reject event for the telemetry sink.
33: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
34: pub struct AdmissionEvent {
35:     /// `admit_accept` or `admit_reject`.
36:     pub operation: String,
37:     /// Category or episodic-type key.
38:     pub candidate_key: String,
39:     /// `semantic` or `episodic`.
40:     pub candidate_kind: String,
41:     /// Score when scoring completed.
42:     pub admission_score: Option<f64>,
43:     /// Why a reject happened.
44:     pub rejection_reason: Option<String>,
45:     /// Isolation key.
46:     pub bank: String,
47:     /// Attribution actor.
48:     pub actor: String,
49:     /// Caller-supplied timestamp.
50:     pub timestamp: String,
51:     /// Secret-masked snapshot preview.
52:     pub preview: Value,
53: }
54: 
55: /// Telemetry sink for admit/reject events.
56: pub trait EventSink: std::fmt::Debug {
57:     /// Record one admission event.
58:     fn emit(&self, event: AdmissionEvent);
59: }
60: 
61: /// In-memory sink for tests and single-process hosts.
62: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
63: pub struct VecSink {
64:     events: Mutex<Vec<AdmissionEvent>>,
65: }
66: 
67: impl VecSink {
68:     /// Read all recorded events.
69:     #[must_use]
70:     pub fn events(&self) -> Vec<AdmissionEvent> {
71:         self.events.lock().expect("admission sink poisoned").clone()
72:     }
73: }
74: 
75: impl EventSink for VecSink {
76:     fn emit(&self, event: AdmissionEvent) {
77:         self.events
78:             .lock()
79:             .expect("admission sink poisoned")
80:             .push(event);
81:     }
82: }
83: 
84: /// Masked preview of an item for reject events.
85: fn masked_preview(item: &MemoryItem) -> Value {
86:     let snapshot = item
87:         .snapshot
88:         .clone()
89:         .map_or(Value::Null, |s| masked_clone(&s));
90:     let gist = item.gist.as_deref().map(|g| {
91:         let mut short = g.chars().take(160).collect::<String>();
92:         if g.chars().count() > 160 {
93:             short.push('…');
94:         }
95:         scrub_inline_secrets(&short)
96:     });
97:     serde_json::json!({ "snapshot": snapshot, "gist": gist })
98: }
99: 
100: fn emit_decision(
101:     sink: &dyn EventSink,
102:     operation: &str,
103:     candidate: Candidate,
104:     item: &MemoryItem,
105:     ctx: &OpContext,
106:     timestamp: &str,
107:     decision: &Decision,
108: ) {
109:     sink.emit(AdmissionEvent {
110:         operation: operation.into(),
111:         candidate_key: candidate.key().into(),
112:         candidate_kind: candidate.kind().as_str().into(),
113:         admission_score: Some(decision.admission_score),
114:         rejection_reason: decision.rejection_reason.clone(),
115:         bank: ctx.bank.as_str().into(),
116:         actor: ctx.actor.as_str().into(),
117:         timestamp: timestamp.into(),
118:         preview: masked_preview(item),
119:     });
120: }
121: 
122: /// Neighbor/prior fetcher for the gated path (injected; not owned by this crate).
123: ///
124: /// `clio-admission` is pure scoring logic and ships **no** default store adapter.
125: /// Hosts (tests, `clio-write`, MCP) must supply a `SignalSource`. Empty neighbor
126: /// lists are only correct when the bank sample is empty — otherwise novelty
127: /// scores `1.0` and can inflate admission. Store down → `factor_unavailable`.
128: ///
129: /// Scoring text and provenance always come from the item itself (see
130: /// [`candidate_text`]), so a decision can never detach from the bytes being
131: /// persisted.
132: pub trait SignalSource: std::fmt::Debug {
133:     /// Neighbor texts for the novelty signal.
134:     ///
135:     /// # Errors
136:     /// `factor_unavailable` when the store backend is down.
137:     fn neighbor_texts(&self, item: &MemoryItem) -> Result<Vec<String>, AmError>;
138: 
139:     /// Age of the nearest prior in days; `None` means no prior exists.
140:     ///
141:     /// # Errors
142:     /// `factor_unavailable` when the store backend is down.
143:     fn prior_age_days(&self, item: &MemoryItem) -> Result<Option<f64>, AmError>;
144: }
145: 
146: /// Candidate text under test: gist plus snapshot, in that order.
147: ///
148: /// This is the single source of scoring text on the gated path; callers must
149: /// not substitute other text for it.
150: #[must_use]
151: pub fn candidate_text(item: &MemoryItem) -> String {
152:     let gist = item.gist.as_deref().unwrap_or("");
153:     match &item.snapshot {
154:         Some(snapshot) => format!("{gist}\n{snapshot}"),
155:         None => gist.to_owned(),
156:     }
157: }
158: 
159: /// Build scoring inputs for an item from its own content plus store lookups.
160: ///
161: /// # Errors
162: /// `factor_unavailable` when a store lookup fails.
163: pub fn signals_for(item: &MemoryItem, source: &dyn SignalSource) -> Result<SignalInputs, AmError> {
164:     let neighbors = source.neighbor_texts(item).map_err(as_factor_unavailable)?;
165:     let prior_age_days = source.prior_age_days(item).map_err(as_factor_unavailable)?;
166:     Ok(SignalInputs {
167:         text: candidate_text(item),
168:         source_type: item.source_type,
169:         neighbors: Some(neighbors),
170:         prior_age_days,
171:         recency_unavailable: false,
172:     })
173: }
174: 
175: /// Keep an existing `factor_unavailable`, else wrap the backend failure.
176: fn as_factor_unavailable(e: AmError) -> AmError {
177:     if e.code == ErrorCode::FactorUnavailable {
178:         return e;
179:     }
180:     crate::factors::factor_unavailable(&e.message)
181: }
182: 
183: /// Shared inputs for a gated write: item, signals, attribution, and policy.
184: #[derive(Debug)]
185: pub struct GateRequest<'a> {
186:     /// Item proposed for admission.
187:     pub item: &'a MemoryItem,
188:     /// Bank isolation and actor attribution.
189:     pub ctx: &'a OpContext,
190:     /// Thresholds, priors, weights, and recency `τ`.
191:     pub policy: AdmissionPolicy<'a>,
192:     /// Telemetry sink for accept/reject events.
193:     pub sink: &'a dyn EventSink,
194:     /// Caller-supplied timestamp for events.
195:     pub timestamp: &'a str,
196: }
197: 
198: /// Gated public write: both gates, then the repository create exactly once.
199: ///
200: /// Rejects never touch `write` but are emitted to `sink`. Backend failures
201: /// return `factor_unavailable` with no write and no reject event.
202: ///
203: /// # Errors
204: /// Invalid bank/item/candidate pairing, unavailable factor backends, or
205: /// storage failures from `write`.
206: pub fn gated_create(
207:     req: &GateRequest<'_>,
208:     candidate: Candidate,
209:     source: &dyn SignalSource,
210:     write: &mut dyn FnMut(&MemoryItem) -> Result<(), AmError>,
211: ) -> Result<Decision, AmError> {
212:     if req.ctx.bank.as_str().is_empty() {
213:         return Err(AmError::new(ErrorCode::MissingBank, "bank is required"));
214:     }
215:     if req.timestamp.is_empty() {
216:         return Err(AmError::new(
217:             ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
218:             "timestamp is required",
219:         ));
220:     }
221:     req.item.validate()?;
222:     if req.item.kind != candidate.kind() {
223:         return Err(AmError::new(
224:             ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
225:             "candidate kind must match item kind (no cross-kind admission)",
226:         ));
227:     }
228:     match candidate {
229:         Candidate::Semantic(category) => {
230:             if req.item.category != Some(category) {
231:                 return Err(AmError::new(
232:                     ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
233:                     "candidate category must match item category (no threshold shopping)",
234:                 ));
235:             }
236:         }
237:         Candidate::Episodic(tag) => {
238:             if req.item.episodic_type != Some(tag) {
239:                 return Err(AmError::new(
240:                     ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
241:                     "candidate episodic_type must match item episodic_type (no threshold shopping)",
242:                 ));
243:             }
244:         }
245:     }
246:     let signals = signals_for(req.item, source)?;
247:     let decision = decide(candidate, &signals, &req.policy)?;
248:     if decision.pass {
249:         let mut admitted = req.item.clone();
250:         admitted.admission_score = Some(decision.admission_score);
251:         write(&admitted)?;
252:         emit_decision(
253:             req.sink,
254:             "admit_accept",
255:             candidate,
256:             &admitted,
257:             req.ctx,
258:             req.timestamp,
259:             &decision,
260:         );
261:     } else {
262:         emit_decision(
263:             req.sink,
264:             "admit_reject",
265:             candidate,
266:             req.item,
267:             req.ctx,
268:             req.timestamp,
269:             &decision,
270:         );
271:     }
272:     Ok(decision)
273: }
274: 
275: /// Gated write from raw discriminator strings; unknown categories or types
276: /// become logged rejections without writes.
277: ///
278: /// # Errors
279: /// Same as [`gated_create`], plus structurally invalid `kind` values.
280: pub fn gated_create_raw(
281:     req: &GateRequest<'_>,
282:     kind: &str,
283:     key: &str,
284:     source: &dyn SignalSource,
285:     write: &mut dyn FnMut(&MemoryItem) -> Result<(), AmError>,
286: ) -> Result<Decision, AmError> {
287:     if kind == "semantic" {
288:         if let Ok(category) = SemanticCategory::parse(key) {
289:             return gated_create(req, Candidate::Semantic(category), source, write);
290:         }
291:         let decision = gate_reject("category", key, "not in whitelist");
292:         emit_gate_reject(
293:             req.sink,
294:             kind,
295:             key,
296:             req.item,
297:             req.ctx,
298:             req.timestamp,
299:             &decision,
300:         );
301:         return Ok(decision);
302:     }
303:     if kind == "episodic" {
304:         if let Ok(tag) = EpisodicType::parse(key) {
305:             return gated_create(req, Candidate::Episodic(tag), source, write);
306:         }
307:         let decision = gate_reject("episodic_type", key, "not in allowlist");
308:         emit_gate_reject(
309:             req.sink,
310:             kind,
311:             key,
312:             req.item,
313:             req.ctx,
314:             req.timestamp,
315:             &decision,
316:         );
317:         return Ok(decision);
318:     }
319:     Err(AmError::new(
320:         ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
321:         format!("kind must be semantic|episodic, got `{kind}`"),
322:     ))
323: }
324: 
325: fn emit_gate_reject(
326:     sink: &dyn EventSink,
327:     kind: &str,
328:     key: &str,
329:     item: &MemoryItem,
330:     ctx: &OpContext,
331:     timestamp: &str,
332:     decision: &Decision,
333: ) {
334:     sink.emit(AdmissionEvent {
335:         operation: "admit_reject".into(),
336:         candidate_key: key.into(),
337:         candidate_kind: kind.into(),
338:         admission_score: Some(decision.admission_score),
339:         rejection_reason: decision.rejection_reason.clone(),
340:         bank: ctx.bank.as_str().into(),
341:         actor: ctx.actor.as_str().into(),
342:         timestamp: timestamp.into(),
343:         preview: masked_preview(item),
344:     });
345: }

68: 
69:     /// Parse an episodic candidate; unknown tags are an error here and a
70:     /// logged rejection through [`decide_raw`].
71:     ///
72:     /// # Errors
73:     /// Unknown episodic-type strings.
74:     pub fn parse_episodic(raw: &str) -> Result<Self, AmError> {
75:         Ok(Self::Episodic(EpisodicType::parse(raw)?))
76:     }
77: }
78: 
79: /// Raw signal inputs for one scoring run.
80: ///
81: /// Hand-built inputs are for previews, tests, and explicit scoring calls.
82: /// Gated writes must derive these from the item through a [`SignalSource`]
83: /// (see `gated`), so the scored text can never detach from the persisted bytes.
84: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
85: pub struct SignalInputs {
86:     /// Candidate text for utility, confidence, and novelty signals.
87:     pub text: String,
88:     /// Provenance for the confidence signal.
89:     pub source_type: Option<clio_types::SourceType>,
90:     /// Neighbor texts for novelty; `None` means the store backend is down.
91:     pub neighbors: Option<Vec<String>>,
92:     /// Age of the nearest prior in days; `None` means no prior exists.
93:     pub prior_age_days: Option<f64>,
94:     /// Set when the recency backend itself is down (distinct from no prior).
95:     pub recency_unavailable: bool,
96: }
97: 
98: /// Five scored factors in `w1…w5` order.
99: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
100: pub struct FactorBreakdown {
101:     /// Future utility.
102:     pub utility: f64,
103:     /// Factual confidence.
104:     pub confidence: f64,
105:     /// Semantic novelty.
106:     pub novelty: f64,
107:     /// Temporal recency.
108:     pub recency: f64,
109:     /// Content-type prior.
110:     pub type_prior: f64,
111: }
112: 
113: impl FactorBreakdown {
114:     fn as_array(self) -> [f64; 5] {
115:         [
116:             self.utility,
117:             self.confidence,
118:             self.novelty,
119:             self.recency,
120:             self.type_prior,
121:         ]
122:     }
123: 
124:     fn zero() -> Self {
125:         Self {
126:             utility: 0.0,
127:             confidence: 0.0,
128:             novelty: 0.0,
129:             recency: 0.0,
130:             type_prior: 0.0,
131:         }
132:     }
133: }
134: 
135: /// Admit/reject outcome; rejections carry a machine-readable reason.
136: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
137: pub struct Decision {
138:     /// True when the score cleared `θ_admit`.
139:     pub pass: bool,
140:     /// Weighted score in `[0, 1]` (`0.0` for gate rejections).
141:     pub admission_score: f64,
142:     /// Per-factor signals.
143:     pub factors: FactorBreakdown,
144:     /// Set when `pass` is false.
145:     pub rejection_reason: Option<String>,
146: }
147: 
148: /// Score one candidate: gate, then five factors, then threshold.
149: ///
150: /// # Errors
151: /// `factor_unavailable` when a required signal backend is down.
152: pub fn decide(
153:     candidate: Candidate,
154:     signals: &SignalInputs,
155:     policy: &AdmissionPolicy<'_>,
156: ) -> Result<Decision, AmError> {
157:     let neighbors = signals
158:         .neighbors
159:         .as_ref()
160:         .ok_or_else(|| factor_unavailable("novelty neighbor store"))?;
161:     if signals.recency_unavailable {
162:         return Err(factor_unavailable("recency store"));
163:     }
164:     let factors = FactorBreakdown {
165:         utility: clamp01(utility_score(&signals.text)),
166:         confidence: clamp01(confidence_score(signals.source_type, &signals.text)),
167:         novelty: novelty_jaccard(&signals.text, neighbors),
168:         recency: recency_decay(signals.prior_age_days, policy.recency_tau_days()),
169:         type_prior: clamp01(policy.prior_for(candidate.key())),
170:     };
171:     let score = weighted_score(policy.weights(), factors.as_array());
172:     let threshold = policy.threshold_for(candidate.key());
173:     if score >= threshold {
174:         Ok(Decision {
175:             pass: true,
176:             admission_score: score,
177:             factors,
178:             rejection_reason: None,
179:         })
180:     } else {
181:         Ok(Decision {
182:             pass: false,
183:             admission_score: score,
184:             factors,
185:             rejection_reason: Some(format!(
186:                 "score {score:.3} < theta {threshold:.3} for `{}`",
187:                 candidate.key()
188:             )),
189:         })
190:     }
191: }
192: 
193: pub(crate) fn gate_reject(kind: &str, key: &str, reason: &str) -> Decision {
194:     Decision {
195:         pass: false,
196:         admission_score: 0.0,
197:         factors: FactorBreakdown::zero(),
198:         rejection_reason: Some(format!("{kind} gate: {reason} for `{key}`")),
199:     }
200: }
201: 
202: /// Score from raw discriminator strings; unknown categories or types become
203: /// logged rejections instead of parse errors.
204: ///
205: /// # Errors
206: /// Only for structurally invalid `kind` values or unavailable factor backends.
207: pub fn decide_raw(
208:     kind: &str,
209:     key: &str,
210:     signals: &SignalInputs,
211:     policy: &AdmissionPolicy<'_>,
212: ) -> Result<Decision, AmError> {
213:     match kind {
214:         "semantic" => match SemanticCategory::parse(key) {
215:             Ok(category) => decide(Candidate::Semantic(category), signals, policy),
216:             Err(_) => Ok(gate_reject("category", key, "not in whitelist")),
217:         },
218:         "episodic" => match EpisodicType::parse(key) {
219:             Ok(tag) => decide(Candidate::Episodic(tag), signals, policy),
220:             Err(_) => Ok(gate_reject("episodic_type", key, "not in allowlist")),
221:         },
222:         other => Err(AmError::new(
223:             ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
224:             format!("kind must be semantic|episodic, got `{other}`"),
225:         )),
226:     }
227: }

230: ///

232: /// Same as [`decide`]; never writes.

234:     candidate: Candidate,
235:     signals: &SignalInputs,
236:     policy: &AdmissionPolicy<'_>,
237: ) -> Result<Decision, AmError> {
238:     decide(candidate, signals, policy)
239: }

248:     signals: &SignalInputs,

250: ) -> Result<Decision, AmError> {

5: //! # Responsibility

24: use clio_types::{AmError, ErrorCode, SourceType};

26: 
27: /// Clamp a signal into `[0, 1]`; non-finite values become `0.0`.
28: #[must_use]
29: pub fn clamp01(value: f64) -> f64 {
30:     if !value.is_finite() {
31:         return 0.0;
32:     }
33:     value.clamp(0.0, 1.0)
34: }
35: 
36: /// Structured error when a required signal backend is unavailable.
37: ///
38: /// Callers must not write and must not emit a reject event for this error.
39: #[must_use]
40: pub fn factor_unavailable(what: &str) -> AmError {
41:     AmError::new(
42:         ErrorCode::FactorUnavailable,
43:         format!("factor_unavailable: {what}"),
44:     )
45: }
46: 
47: /// Future utility from explicit markers: preference/decision/constraint/task
48: /// markers score high, one-off chatter scores low, everything else is neutral.
49: #[must_use]
50: pub fn utility_score(text: &str) -> f64 {
51:     const HIGH: &[&str] = &[
52:         "prefer",
53:         "decision",
54:         "decided",
55:         "constraint",
56:         "must",
57:         "require",
58:         "task",
59:         "todo",
60:         "goal",
61:         "policy",
62:     ];
63:     const CHATTER: &[&str] = &[
64:         "hi", "hello", "hey", "thanks", "thank", "ok", "okay", "bye", "yes", "no",
65:     ];
66:     let lower = text.to_ascii_lowercase();
67:     if HIGH.iter().any(|m| lower.contains(m)) {
68:         return 0.9;
69:     }
70:     let words: Vec<&str> = lower
71:         .split(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric())
72:         .filter(|w| !w.is_empty())
73:         .collect();
74:     if text.trim().len() < 24 && words.iter().any(|w| CHATTER.contains(w)) {
75:         return 0.15;
76:     }
77:     0.5
78: }

81: /// ones, and speculative markers cap the score low.
82: #[must_use]
83: pub fn confidence_score(source_type: Option<SourceType>, text: &str) -> f64 {
84:     const SPECULATIVE: &[&str] = &[
85:         "maybe", "perhaps", "possibly", "might", "guess", "probably", "unsure", "not sure",
86:     ];
87:     let base: f64 = match source_type {

100: /// Lowercase alphanumeric word set for the novelty proxy.
101: fn token_set(text: &str) -> BTreeSet<String> {
102:     text.to_ascii_lowercase()
103:         .split(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric())
104:         .filter(|w| !w.is_empty())
105:         .map(str::to_owned)
106:         .collect()
107: }
108: 
109: /// Jaccard similarity of two token sets.
110: ///
111: /// Only called with a non-empty candidate (empty candidates return early in
112: /// [`novelty_jaccard`]), so the union is never empty here.
113: fn jaccard(a: &BTreeSet<String>, b: &BTreeSet<String>) -> f64 {
114:     let inter = a.intersection(b).count();
115:     let union = a.union(b).count();
116:     // Token counts are bounded by input text length, far below 2^53.
117:     #[allow(clippy::cast_precision_loss)]
118:     let (inter, union) = (inter as f64, union as f64);
119:     inter / union
120: }
121: 
122: /// Semantic novelty proxy: `1 - max_jaccard` over neighbor texts.
123: ///
124: /// Empty candidates score `0.0`; with no neighbors the score is `1.0`.
125: /// Exact token-set duplicates score `0.0`.
126: #[must_use]
127: pub fn novelty_jaccard(text: &str, neighbors: &[String]) -> f64 {
128:     let candidate = token_set(text);
129:     if candidate.is_empty() {
130:         return 0.0;
131:     }
132:     if neighbors.is_empty() {
133:         return 1.0;
134:     }
135:     let best = neighbors
136:         .iter()
137:         .map(|n| jaccard(&candidate, &token_set(n)))
138:         .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max);
139:     clamp01(1.0 - best)
140: }
141: 
142: /// Temporal recency: `exp(-age_days / tau_days)`; no prior scores `1.0`.
143: #[must_use]
144: pub fn recency_decay(prior_age_days: Option<f64>, tau_days: f64) -> f64 {
145:     let Some(age) = prior_age_days else {
146:         return 1.0;
147:     };
148:     if tau_days <= 0.0 || !tau_days.is_finite() {
149:         return 0.0;
150:     }
151:     clamp01((-age.max(0.0) / tau_days).exp())
152: }
153: 
154: /// Weighted admission score from the five factors in `w1…w5` order.
155: #[must_use]
156: pub fn weighted_score(weights: [f64; 5], factors: [f64; 5]) -> f64 {
157:     clamp01(
158:         weights[0] * factors[0]
159:             + weights[1] * factors[1]
160:             + weights[2] * factors[2]
161:             + weights[3] * factors[3]
162:             + weights[4] * factors[4],
163:     )
164: }

.DEFAULT_GOAL := help

CARGO  ?= cargo
BIN    := am
PROFILE ?= local-rft

# Prefer rustup's llvm-tools when Homebrew rustc is first on PATH without llvm-cov.

build compile:

test:

lint:
	$(CARGO) clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

fmt:
	$(CARGO) fmt --all

check: fmt lint test

run:
	$(CARGO) run --locked --bin $(BIN)

# --- coverage (requires: cargo install cargo-llvm-cov; rustup component add llvm-tools-preview) ---

		printf 'Open: %s\n' '$(COV_DIR)/html/index.html'
